title: The ceremony leaves both PIN digests on the coordinator, and the coordinator `DUR-1` claims silence against can test every entered PIN with them
description:
Type: bug. Proposed priority: P2 (the silence claim fails against the adversary it names, in a
default deployment). Kind: requirement and Operator procedure; the fix adds one Operator step
before funding. No node, wire or gate change.

The setup ceremony runs on the coordinator, and copies of both PIN digests stay there: the ceremony
input, `ceremony-state.json`, every `node-<id>.toml` of the sealed set, and any staging residue.
No requirement destroys them, and the backup move of `OPS-24` does not reach them all. At the
wrench, whoever holds the coordinator receives each PIN the user enters. One Argon2 evaluation
against a digest on the same disk tells whether it is the duress PIN, before the request is
relayed. `DUR-1` claims silence against exactly this adversary: one "holding the coordinator and
the physical scene but no node". No exception in `SEC-10` covers a digest holder.

**Evidence** (all at `4fea1bd`)

- The ceremony runs on the coordinator. `MAN-24`'s table: "the coordinator | `assemble`" and "the
  coordinator | `finalize`".
- The copies there:
  - `MAN-27`: `assemble` "MUST take a ceremony input naming bundle PATHS — never inline keys — plus
    the hot descriptor, the two PIN digests". `WIR-14`'s example input carries `pin_normal_hash`
    and `pin_duress_hash` inline. No requirement gives that file a mode or a removal rule.
  - `MAN-33`: "one `node-<id>.toml` per node, **owner-only**, because it carries both PIN digests
    and the backend credential".
  - `MAN-32`: "Every artifact is re-derivable from `ceremony-state.json`, which `finalize` never
    modifies." So the state holds what the node configurations hold.
  - `OPR-80`: an interrupted finalize can leave its staging directory "holding the same coordinator
    key and node secrets as the sealed output"; the documentation must "tell the Operator to
    inspect and remove it".
- Nothing removes them. `OPS-24`: "The sealed backup set (`MAN-33`) MUST be moved off the
  coordinator to storage the Operator controls." `MAN-33`'s backup files carry no PIN digest, and
  `ceremony-state.json` is not in `MAN-33`'s list. The only destruction rule is `MAN-36`'s: "the
  operator MUST destroy the paper preimage". File modes (`MAN-29`, `MAN-33`, `MAN-34`, `MAN-40`)
  stop other local users, not the host's holder. `OPR-10`'s "MUST NOT read node configuration
  files" binds the operator program, not the host.
- The coordinator has every PIN. `DOM-4`: the PIN "is entered per request, relayed in the request
  body, and discarded".
- The test is cheap. `MAN-20`: the two digests are Argon2id PHC strings, "one normal and one duress,
  each with its own salt". `MAN-21` refuses only values above "`m > 262 144` KiB, `t > 10`, or
  `p > 16`"; there is no floor. `DEF-11` measured "a 199 ms one-Argon2 target effect". A PIN in hand
  needs no search, so PIN entropy does not help (`SEC-26`: "Higher-entropy PINs are defence in
  depth, not load-bearing").
- The claim and its exceptions:
  - `DUR-1`: "Silence is claimed against an adversary holding the coordinator and the physical scene
    but no node, subject to `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise"; a node sees the PIN."
  - `DOM-2`: that coordinator turns hostile "AT the moment of coercion, holding the coordinator
    auth key but no history of the normal PIN".
  - `SEC-10`: "It is not a claim that no adversary can learn the PIN class: a compromised node sees
    the PIN in plaintext, and a coordinator compromised before the wrench reads and substitutes
    it."
  - `ADR-0012` accepts "a compromised node offline-bruting the hashes"; a node is "A daemon holding
    exactly one federation signing key and one policy engine" (`01-domain-model.md`).
- The funds. With a digest the coercer can drop a duress request before relaying it and demand the
  other PIN. `SEC-54` row 9 says "Denial: duress sweeps to the escape wallet at `T`, Lockdown
  follows"; row 8 says "duress is nullified by PIN substitution". `SEC-54`'s secrets are `DOM-10`'s,
  and the digests have no letter among them, although `SEC-1` lists "the two PIN digests" among the
  secondary assets.

**Review**

Four readers (A–D) read the texts at `4fea1bd` independently, in two rounds.

- Round 1, the question:
  - The claim fails against its own named adversary: 4–0. The coordinator can hold digest copies:
    4–0. `ADR-0012` excludes a digest holder: 0–4.
  - The finding's first framing was a node key leak that also copies the configuration. All four
    found it only partly right. On a node host a disk image, or rescue mode (which reboots), yields
    neither the key nor the configuration, which live on tmpfs (`OPS-53`, `STO-1`); only access to
    the running host yields both. The copies on the coordinator hold digests and no key.
  - The fund outcome moves toward row 8: 4–0, conditionally. The coercer must still obtain the
    normal PIN. Hot budget, allowlist and Hold still apply. B, C and D: outside `SEC-54` as written.
  - The fix: A and B would narrow the claim in text only, with no behaviour change. C would move
    the copies off the coordinator. D would destroy them, on the reasoning that storage the
    Operator controls can be within reach of a coercer who holds the user.
- Decision: destroy the copies, with a scope sentence for the copies that destruction cannot reach.
- Round 2, the exact text: ready after fixes, 4–0. Applied:
  - A drill-restore exception for `OPS-63` was false (B, C, D; A as a broken path). No backup ever
    held a node configuration, and the preimage is gone at first start, so this bead does not change
    what that drill can do. It is dropped.
  - `SEC-28` was cited for a live memory capture; it says "a VPS is never sealed against its
    provider's console and rescue mode" (A). `F40` covers only the image's delivery; the
    configuration's path to a node host is unspecified, and that channel may keep a copy (C, D).
  - "Classifies" overclaimed. One digest tests a PIN against its own role (A).
  - "Every other artifact still can" be re-derived overclaimed: `finalize` renders the entire set,
    node configurations included (A, B, C, D).
  - `ceremony-state.json` also carries audit records: the timelock confirmation (`OPR-78`) and
    `--allow-shared-parent` (`MAN-40`). A copy with the digests removed is kept (C, D).
  - Deleting a file on a disk that stays in service does not destroy it. The standard below
    merges A's, C's and D's wordings (B: feasible as first written).
  - Added: aborted or repeated ceremony runs, including an incomplete `sealed/` (D); the
    default-lifecycle qualifier (D); `DOM-2` (C, D).
- Not decided here: A, B and C would also reword `OPS-25` and `OPS-63`'s node-restore step to say
  that no node can be restored. D would leave them. That tension between `OPS-25`'s "restores a
  node" and `STO-1`'s "A dead node never rejoins" predates this bead.

**Proposed text**

1. `OPS-35`, replacing it:

   > **OPS-35** Once a node is up and sealed, destroy its paper preimage (`MAN-36`). After the last
   > node start (`MAN-36`) and before the vault is first funded (`OPS-36`), the Operator MUST destroy
   > every copy of either PIN digest that is not on a node host: every `node-<id>.toml` of the
   > sealed set and every copy of one made to reach a node host; the ceremony input of `MAN-27`;
   > `ceremony-state.json`, once a copy with both digest fields removed is kept for the records it
   > carries (`OPR-78`, `MAN-40`); the output of enrolment (`MAN-20`); the output of every aborted or
   > repeated `assemble` or `finalize`, including staging residue (`OPR-80`) and an incomplete
   > `sealed/` removed under `MAN-32`; and any copy left from an earlier vault whose PINs are reused.
   > A copy is destroyed only when the medium that held it was volatile storage, with swap and
   > hibernation off, that has since been cleared, or has been cryptographically erased or
   > physically destroyed; deleting or rewriting a file on a disk that stays in service does not
   > destroy it. No copy is kept as a backup. Under the default lifecycle (`OPS-62` (a)) nothing
   > needs one: a node starts exactly once (`STO-1`), a sealed vault is never reconfigured (`OPS-1`),
   > and a rotation needs neither the old PINs nor their digests (`OPS-30`). A copy is an offline
   > test: each digest checks a PIN against its enrolled role in one Argon2 evaluation, and whoever
   > holds the coordinator at the wrench (`DOM-2`) sees every PIN the user enters (`DOM-4`).

2. `OPS-24`, replacing it:

   > **OPS-24** The backup set — `MAN-33`'s `backup/` files — MUST be moved off the coordinator to
   > storage the Operator controls. The node configurations are not part of it: they carry the PIN
   > digests, and `OPS-35` destroys them. The coordinator auth secret MUST be stored separately from
   > the descriptor.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug

**Summary:** Before the vault is first funded, the Operator destroys every copy of either PIN digest
that is not on a node host (`OPS-35`), the backup set leaves the node configurations out
(`OPS-24`), and `MAN-32` agrees; `SEC-10` names a "digest premise", that the adversary holds no
copy of either PIN digest, and every statement of the silence scope that edits 5 to 11 name
carries it; `ADR-0021` records the decision, which narrows the current application of
`ADR-0012`'s "Silence model A" for a holder of a copy, with `ADR-0012` not edited.

**Current behavior:**
The setup ceremony runs on the coordinator and leaves copies of both PIN digests there: the
ceremony input of `MAN-27`, `ceremony-state.json`, every `node-<id>.toml` of the sealed set, and
any staging residue. No requirement destroys them, and `OPS-24`'s move of the backup set does not
reach them all. Whoever holds the coordinator at the wrench receives each PIN the user enters and
can test it against a digest in one Argon2 evaluation before relaying it, yet `DUR-1` claims
silence against an adversary "holding the coordinator and the physical scene but no node". The
description has the evidence.

**Desired behavior:** these twelve edits, as written.

1. `OPS-35`, replacing it:

   > **OPS-35** Once a node is up and sealed, destroy its paper preimage (`MAN-36`). After the last
   > node start (`MAN-36`) and before the vault is first funded (`OPS-36`), the Operator MUST destroy
   > every copy of either PIN digest that is not on a node host, including: every `node-<id>.toml` of the
   > sealed set and every copy of one made to reach a node host; the ceremony input of `MAN-27`;
   > `ceremony-state.json`, once its audit records (`OPR-78`'s confirmation, `MAN-40`'s flag) are
   > kept in a file that holds no digest and no secret; the output of enrolment (`MAN-20`); the
   > output of every aborted or repeated `assemble` or `finalize`, including staging residue
   > (`OPR-80`) and an incomplete `sealed/` removed under `MAN-32`; any copy left from an earlier
   > vault whose PINs are reused; and every snapshot, backup or synchronised copy of any of these.
   > A copy is destroyed only when the medium that held it was volatile storage, with swap and
   > hibernation off, that has since been cleared, or has been cryptographically erased or
   > physically destroyed; deleting or rewriting a file on a disk that stays in service does not
   > destroy it. No copy is kept as a backup. Under the default lifecycle (`OPS-62` (a))
   > nothing needs one: a node starts exactly once (`STO-1`), a sealed vault is never reconfigured
   > (`OPS-1`), and a rotation needs neither the old PINs nor their digests (`OPS-30`). A copy is
   > an offline test: each digest checks a PIN against its enrolled role in one Argon2 evaluation,
   > and whoever holds the coordinator at the wrench (`DOM-2`) sees every PIN the user enters
   > (`DOM-4`).

2. `OPS-24`, replacing it:

   > **OPS-24** The backup set — `MAN-33`'s `backup/` files — MUST be moved off the coordinator to
   > storage the Operator controls. The node configurations are not part of it: they carry the PIN
   > digests, and `OPS-35` destroys them. The coordinator auth secret MUST be stored separately from
   > the descriptor.

3. `MAN-32`, replacing "Every artifact is re-derivable from `ceremony-state.json`, which `finalize`
   never modifies." with: "Every artifact is re-derivable from `ceremony-state.json`, which
   `finalize` never modifies, until `OPS-35` destroys it before funding. The file of audit records
   `OPS-35` keeps in its place is not a ceremony state: it holds no digest and no secret."

4. `SEC-10`, replacing "It is not a claim that no adversary can learn the PIN class: a compromised
   node sees the PIN in plaintext, and a coordinator compromised before the wrench reads and
   substitutes it." with: "It is not a claim that no adversary can learn the PIN class: a
   compromised node sees the PIN in plaintext, a coordinator compromised before the wrench reads
   and substitutes it, and a holder of a copy of either PIN digest can test offline whether a PIN
   it holds is the one enrolled in that digest's role. Its **digest premise** is that the
   adversary holds no copy of either PIN digest. `OPS-35` requires every copy off the node hosts
   to be destroyed before funding; that procedure does not establish the premise, and no theorem
   does. Destruction cannot revoke a copy already taken, and the claim does not reach a copy that
   rule cannot destroy: one acquired from a node host through provider access (`SEC-28`), or one
   kept or intercepted by whatever carried a configuration to a node host, which the set does not
   specify (`F40` covers only the image)."

5. `DUR-1`, replacing its last sentence with: "Silence is claimed against an adversary holding the
   coordinator and the physical scene but no node, subject to `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise"
   and "digest premise"; a node sees the PIN, and a holder of a digest copy can test one
   (`SEC-10`)."

6. `OVR-13`, replacing "subject to `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise". Hiding" with "subject to
   `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise" and "digest premise". Hiding".

7. `DOM-2`, replacing "That history boundary depends on `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise"." with
   "That history boundary depends on `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise" and "digest premise"."

8. `SEC-54`, appending to the preamble after "holds `U` while the user key is software.": "The PIN
   digests have no letter: `OPS-35` requires every copy off the node hosts to be destroyed before
   funding. A coercer who holds one anyway can test the PIN offered before relaying it and withhold
   a duress request, and once it has the normal PIN it nullifies duress as in row 8; silence is
   not claimed against it (`SEC-10`)."

9. `CONTEXT.md`, **SILENCE**, replacing "It assumes no node ran a compromised release while the
   current PINs were in use." with "It assumes no node ran a compromised release while the current
   PINs were in use, and that the adversary holds no copy of either PIN digest (`SEC-10`)."

10. `executive-summary.md`'s silence paragraph, replacing `in use". Under that premise, silence
    holds` with `in use", and on its "digest premise", that the adversary holds no copy of either
    PIN digest. Under both premises, silence holds`.

11. The module docstrings:
    - `BtcPolicy.Silence`, after "or model PIN history retained on a coordinator by such a
      release.": "Applying it is equally conditional on `SEC-10`'s "digest premise", that the
      adversary holds no copy of either PIN digest, since a copy tests a PIN against the table;
      these proofs do not establish that premise either."
    - `BtcPolicy.Silence` and `BtcPolicy.Alerts`, "a compromised node or failure of `SEC-10`'s
      "release-history premise"" becomes "… "release-history premise" or "digest premise"".
    - `BtcPolicy.Silence`, *What is not claimed at all*: "a compromised node or a coordinator
      compromised before the wrench" becomes "a compromised node, a holder of a PIN-digest copy or
      a coordinator compromised before the wrench".
    - `BtcPolicy.Alerts`, after "cover PIN history a compromised release left on the
      coordinator.": "Application to SILENCE also assumes `SEC-10`'s "digest premise", which queue
      equality does not establish either."

12. `ADR-0021`, a dated decision after "Decision 2026-10-05: compromised releases and predecessor
    data":

    > ## Decision 2026-10-21: PIN-digest copies
    >
    > Accepted: `OPS-35` requires every copy of either PIN digest off the node hosts to be destroyed
    > before funding, and `SEC-10` owns the "digest premise", that the adversary holds no copy of
    > either PIN digest. The scope references are `OVR-13`, `DOM-2` and `DUR-1`; the `SEC-54`
    > preamble records that silence is not claimed against a holder of a copy. A copy is an offline
    > test: its holder can test whether a PIN it holds is the one enrolled in that digest's role,
    > and whoever holds the coordinator at the wrench sees every PIN the user enters. This
    > decision narrows the current application of `ADR-0012`'s unnumbered "Silence model A"
    > threat-model bullet: silence is not claimed against a holder of a copy of either PIN digest,
    > even one "who has compromised **no node**". `ADR-0012` remains unchanged as the historical
    > design record.
    >
    > Rejected: narrowing the claim in text alone, which leaves the copies on the coordinator, where
    > whoever holds it at the wrench can test every PIN the user enters; and moving the copies to
    > storage the Operator controls, which can be within reach of a coercer who holds the user.

Edits 5 and 6 leave "but no node" alone; `bps-xyu` owns that phrase. With edit 4 in place, a key
copier who also took a node host's digests is outside the claim whichever way `bps-xyu` goes.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `OPS-35` requires the destruction and states the standard, and `OPS-24` leaves the node
      configurations out of the backup set (edits 1, 2).
- [ ] `MAN-32`'s re-derivability sentence agrees with `OPS-35` (edit 3).
- [ ] `SEC-10` names the "digest premise"; `DUR-1`, `OVR-13`, `DOM-2`, the `SEC-54` preamble,
      `CONTEXT.md`'s **SILENCE** entry, `executive-summary.md`'s silence paragraph and the module
      docstrings of `BtcPolicy.Silence` and `BtcPolicy.Alerts` carry it (edits 4 to 11).
- [ ] `ADR-0021` records the decision (edit 12). `ADR-0012` is checked and never edited.
- [ ] Every other statement of the silence scope has been checked against the digest premise,
      `CONTEXT.md`'s "silence" usage rule and `SEC-54` row 16 among them, and only what disagrees
      has changed. The closing comment lists what was checked and what changed.
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`, unpiped and redirected to a file, exits 0.

**Out of scope:**
- No node, wire or gate behaviour changes, and the formal Silence model is not in question.
- A leak of a node key is not shown to carry the configuration. On a node host a disk image, or
  rescue mode, yields neither.
- "In seconds" is not claimed as a bound: `MAN-21` sets only ceilings, and `DEF-11`'s figure is one
  measurement.
- The fund outcome against a digest holder is row 8's, "Bounded theft", not unbounded theft: the
  coercer must still obtain the normal PIN, and the allowlist, Hot budget and Hold still apply.
- A node host's own copy stays, and is not addressed beyond edit 4's exclusion.
- If `OPS-62` chooses (b), how a restart gets its configuration is that ADR's to decide. `OPS-62`
  already requires it to "explicitly supersede or amend every document it contradicts".
- `OPS-25` and `OPS-63` are unchanged (`bps-ay1`). `SEC-54` row 9's attacker cell is `bps-amt`'s,
  and its record condition is `bps-xyu`'s (edit 10). "but no node" in `DUR-1` and `OVR-13`, which
  `ADR-0028` quotes, is `bps-xyu`'s.

**HARD STOPS** (owner-only; never settle by consultation):
1. The remedy is the owner's: "destroy the copies, with a scope sentence for the copies that
   destruction cannot reach" (description). If a reviewer asks to keep a copy, to move the copies
   to storage the Operator controls, or to narrow the claim in text alone, stop and report.
2. `ADR-0012` is not edited (owner, 2026-10-21). If an edit seems to need a change to its file,
   stop and report.
3. Edit 12's sentence naming `ADR-0012`'s "Silence model A" as narrowed is the owner's decision. If
   a reviewer asks to drop it, or to reword it so that it no longer names that bullet, stop and
   report.
4. The opening sentences of `README.md` (lines 4–5 at `9dd1ac1`), `00-overview.md` (19–21),

5. If an edit, as written, makes false a theorem statement, an ADR decision or a requirement this

title: Copies gate per-file hit count misses a swap: a malformed copy plus a new valid copy in one file is green
description:
`tools/check_copies.py:265-266` holds the corpus-wide copies scan to a per-file HIT COUNT baseline (`tools/copies-baseline.json`): red on a fall, red on an unrecorded rise. A count cannot see a swap: when one existing copy becomes unrecognizable and a new valid copy is added in the same file, the per-file count is unchanged and the malformed copy escapes.

Reviewer D's example (unverified, verify first): in `README.md` change `(2 − 1/t)` to `(3 − one/t)` and append a valid `(2 − 1/t)` elsewhere in the same file; the gate exits 0, although AGENTS.md says an inline figure is held to the value its declaration emits.

Repair, smallest that works: instead of (or beside) the per-file count, detect formula-LIKE copies that no owner regex matches — e.g. for each entry keep a looser "shape" regex (the same pattern with the operands wildcarded, as the existing "stopped matching" check already does per entry) and refuse any hit of the shape that the exact pattern does not also match. Do not redesign the baseline file; regenerate it only through `--write` if its format must change, and say so in the commit.

Acceptance criteria:
- The swap mutation above is red, naming the file and the unmatched copy.
- One new negative control in `tools/check_gate_controls.py` (`COPIES`) for the swap, in the existing `text_control` shape (two edits in one file may need a small mutate function).
- KEEP working: every existing copies control still red for its stated reason and the positive control green; `tools/copies-baseline.json` unchanged unless `--write` regenerated it for a stated reason; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green on the final tree.
- Files: `tools/check_copies.py`, `tools/check_gate_controls.py`, `tools/copies-baseline.json` (only if regenerated). No Lean, no Markdown.

Source: reviewer D's review of commit 949d63f (confirmation pass, 2026-09-16). Reviewer A did not report it.

title: POL-20's composed-run exhibit misses a row released one second early or re-timed at exposure, and no exhibit pins a retry's reservation time
description:
Found in the review of `bps-id2` after acceptance (`0f1baf7`, with `84c84da` on top). Evidence:
`/var/tmp/id2-evidence/`.

**What was measured.** Each plant edits one definition in `BtcPolicy/Ledger.lean`. The owning
proofs it breaks are stubbed with `sorry`, the way the negative-control steps in `gates.yml` stub
them. Then `lake build` runs.

- **P5** (`plants/P5_ageOut_boundary.*`): `ageOut` filters with `window - 1` instead of `window`.
  The release at an accepted hot admission then drops a row one second before its interval ends.
  - Stubs: `ageOut_keeps_in_window`, `released_below_ratchet`.
  - The build is green at `0f1baf7` and at `fe61c93` (`base-check/`).
  - `P5_counter.lean`, in the planted tree, derives `False` from `Ledger.countsAt_of_sysRun` on a
    run from `sys0` under `current`.
- **P1** (`plants/P1_markExposed_retime.*`): `markExposed` sets an exposed row's `reservedAt` to
  `Mono.sample 0`.
  - Stubs at `0f1baf7`: `retained_outside_prune_and_admission`, `hasReservation_markExposed`.
  - Stubs at `fe61c93`: `retained_outside_prune_and_admission`.
  - The build is green at both.
  - `P1_counter.lean` derives `False` in the same way.
- **P4** (`plants/P4_retry_retime.*`): a retry of a held commitment re-times its row to the
  retry's sample.
  - Stubs: `liveSum_reserve_le_cap`, `holds_reserve_of_holds`, `hasReservation_reserve`.
  - The build is green at `0f1baf7`.
  - The statement of `Ledger.countsAt_of_sysRun` stays true under it. No exhibit pins `POL-18`'s
    "a retry keeps the original reservation time".
- **The landed control's own plant** (`plants/P0_control.*`) goes red in
  `composed_reservation_counted_with_current` only, as the step asserts.

None of the three is new: P1 and P5 are green at the base too. `bps-id2` added the first theorem

```
/-! ### `POL-20`: a counted row keeps its own reservation time

`composed_reservation_counted_with_current` checks 10 seconds after the first reservation, with
nothing in between. The run below adds a peer's relay that runs the holder decision, a fire pass
that exposes the row, a replay of the same pair under a fresh Carrier, and a wall excursion past
the row's signed expiry and back, with a prune pass at its peak that collects the pair while the
row stays. Its last check runs at exactly the reservation time plus the
window, with the wall past that expiry: only the monotonic disjunct, at its inclusive boundary,
keeps the row (`POL-19`: "a reservation is released when both disjuncts are false"). -/

/-- The first hot spend, fire time 30 and signed expiry 130, and its Escape, accepted at wall and
HotClock 10. -/
def keptSp : Cand := cand 1 hot1 true (some 30) 130
def keptEsc : Cand := cand 2 esc1 false none 130
def keptEnvR : Env := envAt 10 10
def keptAccept : Event := .accept 10 false (Wall.sample 130) keptSp keptEsc

/-- The relay that runs the holder decision at 20, the fire pass at 30, the same pair replayed
under Carrier 20 at 40, the prune pass that collects the pair at wall 500 and HotClock 60, and the
wall back at 50 with HotClock 70. -/
def keptMid : List (Env × Event) :=
  [ (envAt 20 20, .receipt 10 1),
    (envAt 30 30, .firePass),
    (envAt 40 40, .accept 20 false (Wall.sample 150) keptSp keptEsc),
    (envAt 500 60, .prune),
    (envAt 50 70, .tick) ]
def keptPre : List (Env × Event) := (keptEnvR, keptAccept) :: keptMid

/-- The second spend accepted at wall 131 and HotClock 130 = 10 + 120. -/
def keptLast : Env × Event := (envAt 131 130, .accept 30 false (Wall.sample 241) next nextEsc)
def keptRun : Sys :=
  (sysRun Ledger.current cohortCfg Kernel.current sys0 (keptPre ++ [keptLast])).1

/-- At the last check the first row has its commitment, its original reservation time, its signed
expiry and its exposure bit set, and it is counted (`POL-18`: "a retry keeps the original
reservation time"; `SPN-33`: "the ledger retains its original reservation time, expiry and
exposure state independently of candidate residency"). -/
@[req "POL-20"]
theorem composed_row_time_kept_with_current :
    keptRun.led.map (fun r => (r.cid, r.reservedAt, r.expiry, r.exposed)) =
      [(1, Mono.sample 10, Wall.sample 130, true), (5, Mono.sample 130, Wall.sample 241, false)] ∧
    countsAt cohortCfg.window keptSp.id { led := keptRun.led, now := keptLast.1.mono } = true := by
  decide

/-- `countsAt_of_sysRun_with_current` applies to this run: its premises hold across the exposure, the
replay, the prune pass and the wall excursion. -/
@[req "POL-20"]
theorem composed_row_counted_by_theorem_with_current :
    countsAt cohortCfg.window keptSp.id { led := keptRun.led, now := keptLast.1.mono } = true :=
  countsAt_of_sysRun_with_current cohortCfg Kernel.current sys0 keptPre keptLast
    (by simp only [keptPre, keptMid, keptLast, List.cons_append, List.nil_append,
      MonotoneHotClock]; decide)
    [] (keptMid ++ [keptLast]) keptEnvR 10 false (Wall.sample 130) keptSp keptEsc rfl
    (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)

/-! ### `POL-21`: a frozen candidate's refund, at the prune pass that collects it
```

> silently arming a sweep at `T`

> The **sweep track** — combine and broadcast the pre-signed Escape at `T` — is best-effort

title: `ADR-0008` says a compromised node "learns the one pin used in the request it handled, and nothing more" and that an attacker "can never verify which PIN they were given", where `MAN-33` puts both PIN digests in every node's config and `SEC-10` lets a digest holder test a PIN offline
description:
Type: bug. Proposed priority: P3 (a design record that says more than the set; no requirement
changes). Kind: ADR text; direction open. Found by the readers of the 2026-10-23 triage of the
security chapter. All quotes are at `201224c`.

**Owner decision** (verbatim, 2026-10-23): the bundle "Take them (Recommended)", whose item 6 is
"`ADR-0008`:32 gets its own needs-triage bead (4–0, round 2)" and whose item 7 puts
`ADR-0008`:27 in the same bead. Its item 5 leaves the line between them, "a stolen user key alone
can no longer get anything signed", because "alone" makes it true.

`ADR-0008` (`docs/adr/0008-duress-pins-and-lockdown.md`) says two things the set now says are
too strong:

1. In its *Consequences*: "a compromised node learns the one pin used in the request it handled,
   and nothing more (pins are never logged)".
2. In its body, before *Consequences*: "The software is open source, so an attacker knows a duress PIN exists —
   but they can never verify which PIN they were given".

Against both, `MAN-33` says each `node-<id>.toml` is "**owner-only**, because it carries both PIN
digests", and `SEC-10` says "a holder of a copy of either PIN digest can test offline whether a PIN
it holds is the one enrolled in that digest's role". So a compromised node holds both digests, and
an attacker who holds a digest copy can check which PIN they were given.

**Not claimed**

- No direction is chosen here: whether the ADR gets a dated entry, a note, or stays as the
  historical record is triage's call, and an ADR decision is the owner's (`AGENTS.md`, *When the
  set blocks the work*).
- The set does not say a compromised node learns the other PIN: `SEC-10` says a digest holder
  "can test" a PIN it holds.
- The "a stolen user key alone" line is left (the owner's pick above).

Any text the Manager changes after the last review must be disclosed as unreviewed. Closure evidence is checked against the committed tracker; no claim of completed work precedes its evidence.

HARD STOPS, owner-only; never settle by consultation:

1. Any need to depart from R2's exact text, change the protected stolen-user-key consequence, reopen a governing ADR decision, change a requirement/theorem/observation relation, or resolve the independent on-chain or submitted-PIN-alone claims is a stop. Finish independent checks and report the conflict with quoted texts and "needs an owner decision"; do not research alternatives, draft under one reading or weaken a proof.
2. Any edit outside ADR-0008 and this bead's tracker record is a stop. In particular leave every requirement, formal source, gate, workflow and other bead alone. No new bead is part of this bounded correction.
3. A new silent green against the base is a stop for the owner, never a consultation. The four MISS cases above are already known and require literal checking; their existence is not a new finding. Do not change gate strength in this Run.
4. A refused command is reported as refused and never redone by another tool or route. Reviewers run gates, builds, tests and plants only in their own clones carrying the actual reviewed work. title: Decide what authorizes reopening an ADR decision, and whether the decisions agents re-argue need a marker in the ADR (`AGENTS.md`, *An ADR decision is the owner's*)
description:
Type: task. Proposed priority: P3. Kind: process text in `AGENTS.md`, and possibly a convention in
`README.md`'s *Requirement conventions* or in `docs/adr/`; no requirement change, no behaviour
change.

`AGENTS.md`, *An ADR decision is the owner's*, landed with this bead, says an ADR decision changes
only on an owner decision recorded on the bead that lands the change, naming the ADR and the
decision number, and that a brief contradicting a decision without naming it, a reviewer finding,
a Reviewer majority, or a theorem that would prove more easily under the other choice is a stop,
never an authorization.

**Evidence** (all at `dd18bb6`)

- `docs/agents/domain.md` says to flag an ADR conflict rather than override it: "_Contradicts
  ADR-0020 (every confirmed duress Escape is selected), but worth reopening because…_". Nothing
  says who may reopen a decision or what a reopening looks like in the record.
- Five of the 28 ADRs say whose decision they record ("decision by the specification owner");
  the other 23 do not say.
- Owner decisions reach agents through bead comments ("record the owner's decision on
  `bps-svf`", `5f757d8`) and through a brief's HARD STOPS ("owner-only; never settle by
  consultation", `bps-xrv`). Neither is in the ADR the decision lands in.
- Decisions that briefs have had to defend more than once: `ADR-0028` decision 2's
  "`BtcPolicy.Silence.silence` and `BtcPolicy.Silence.silence_initial` prove under every value
  of both fields, the two mixed combinations included, with no premise on either field", which
  `bps-xrv`'s HARD STOP 1 restates; and `SEC-37`'s residual, kept when `F68` was fixed
  (`e50abc5`, "`SEC-37` kept").

Where the rule came from: the Linked Specs convention (`rad:z2HR882B4c4mTdAgdt4SozpdeTuMf`,
`skills/linked-specs-updating/SKILL.md`) keeps a `GATE-*` record for "a major governing
constraint that agents must not change or reverse without returning to the user", and says
"Nothing else authorizes a gate operation: not implementation or documentation work, research,
planning, a recommendation, a conflicting task, the user's selection among options or acceptance
of other work, an agent's judgment or request". The useful part here is the authorization rule,
not the record type: this set's decisions already have a home in `docs/adr/`.

**Questions for the owner**

1. Is the owner decision recorded on the bead enough, or do some decisions need a marker in the
   ADR itself, beside the decision number, that a Reviewer can cite when a brief or a finding
   re-argues them? If a marker: which decisions carry it, starting from the two above.
2. Should every ADR say whose decision it records, as five do?
3. Does an ADR's rejected option bind like its numbered decisions, so that re-proposing it is a
   stop, or only the numbered decisions?

**Not claimed**

- No ADR is claimed to have been changed without an owner decision.
- No new record type, directory or index: the rule attaches to what `docs/adr/` already holds.

**Done when**

1. The owner's answers to the three questions are on this bead.
2. `AGENTS.md`, *An ADR decision is the owner's*, says what the answers say.
3. If a marker is chosen: `README.md`'s *Requirement conventions* or the `docs/adr/` convention
   says what it looks like, the decisions that carry it are marked, and `docs/agents/domain.md`'s
   conflict note points at it.
4. The gate is green unpiped.
close_reason: Rechecked at a7641ef. AGENTS.md says "An ADR decision is the owner's" and "It changes only on an owner decision recorded on the bead that lands the change, naming the ADR and the decision number." It explicitly treats "the ADR rejected what the brief asks for" as a stop and says "a reviewer finding, a Reviewer majority, or a theorem that would prove more easily under the other choice is a stop under the rule above, never an authorization." The authorization and rejected-choice rules are present; the bead alleges no unauthorized ADR change. Additional decision markers or attribution banners would be cosmetic. Closed without inventing answers to optional convention questions or creating a replacement bead.

title: A per-node ladder split leaves only the base Escape completing; SPN-38 and DUR-28 claim cross-node rung agreement
description:
**Correction 2026-10-04, after the first Run's review.** Decision 4's last sentence below ("The
escape-class spend/residual swap (ADR-0016, ADR-0012) can still suppress the residual sweep; keep
that power stated") is wrong and is withdrawn. ADR-0022 removed the escape-class pair: "Every
SpendRequest is now exactly a hot spend plus its Escape", and it removed "the swap in `SEC-21`'s
list". `CHN-23` and `OPR-25` refuse an `(Escape, Escape)` pair, and they stay unchanged. The swap is
history, not a live power. Decisions 1–3 and the rest of decision 4 stand.

Do now, inside this bead:
- `SEC-21`: delete the sentence asserting the swap as a current power.
- `SEC-21` still owns the suppression that other text files under it, and the change must not drop
  that. `16-open-findings.md`'s row "A selected Escape naming an absent or inflated prevout …
  raises every later denominator and can fail every real Escape" is filed as "accepted residual
  inside `SEC-21`'s suppression", and ADR-0020 calls the split-selection denial "inside the
  residual `SEC-21` already grants". State that suppression where it actually comes from: censoring
  or selectively delivering requests, including one whose selected Escape inflates the coverage
  denominator (`DUR-22`), and never from stripping. The denominator contract does not change.
- `DUR-10` and ADR-0020: ground "choosing which selected Escape confirms" in `SEC-21`'s "censor,
  selectively deliver", not in the stripping sentence. ADR-0020's Consequences quote `SEC-21` with
  words it no longer contains (the swap sentence); quote what `SEC-21` now says.
- ADR-0016's "A separate escape-class role-order residual is accepted" section, and anything else
  the first Run added about the swap: mark them as historical and withdrawn by ADR-0022, not as a
  current residual. ADR-0012's swap mention gets the same treatment if it reads as current.
- Re-grep for "swap", "spend/residual", "role-order" and "suppress" across the Markdown, ADRs and
  Lean docstrings, and reconcile every active reference.

The first Run's commits (924be5c, fa3ddb5, 8a83a8d) stay as they are: add commits and rewrite
nothing. Land this as one commit plus a `beads: close bps-444` commit.

**Decided 2026-10-04 (owner).** Implement as recorded; do not reopen. This block supersedes the
original finding below where they disagree, including its "Owner decision wanted", its "Also
unverified" section and its "Done when".

1. **Nodes do not recompute `CHN-17`.** ADR-0016 §4a and `MAN-13`'s "nodes never enforce it"
   stand, and the per-node ladder split is an accepted residual. Record the reasons in ADR-0016:
   ADR-0012's "Nodes validate the escape; they do NOT build it"; a gate-25 refusal stages nothing
   and so arms nothing, so any disagreement between the composer's and a node's derivation would
   leave an honest duress request unarmed; and with decision 2, every stripping outcome is bounded
   at the base.
2. **Every Escape transaction signals.** The base and every rung, with or without a ladder, set
   every input's `nSequence` to `0xfffffffd`, as refresh (`CHN-18`) and claw-back (`CHN-35`)
   already do. The non-signalling form is withdrawn. Signalling only permits a replacement and
   never blocks relay or confirmation, and under full-RBF (`CHN-15`'s own text) the mark buys
   nothing. The ladderless `0xffffffff` rule is what made a stripped base unbroadcastable.
3. **Gate 25 refuses an Escape transaction that does not signal**, base or rung, as
   `escape:bump_ladder`, the code `CNF-142` already gives `nSequence` faults. `DUR-23` drops its
   `nSequence` condition: ingress owns it.
4. **Consequence.** Stripping rungs, alike on every node or differently per node, only downgrades
   the `T`-time sweep, at worst to the base Escape when the base is admissible. The escape-class
   spend/residual swap (ADR-0016, ADR-0012) can still suppress the residual sweep; keep that power
   stated.

**Lands on** (every site found by grep; re-grep before closing):
- `CHN-15`: one rule, every Escape transaction at `0xfffffffd`; delete the opt-in-relay sentence.
  The "unlike the Escape (`CHN-15`) it never has the non-signalling form" asides in `CHN-18` and
  `CHN-35`. `OPR-25`'s "ladderless Escape carries `nSequence` `0xffffffff`".
- `SPN-27` names the signalling check and its refusal; `DUR-23` as in decision 3.
- `CNF-142`'s `nSequence` sentence; `CNF-118`'s "a ladderless Escape carries `0xffffffff`".
- `SEC-21`: stripping only downgrades, at worst to the base, whether alike or per node; ground any
  remaining "suppress" in the spend/residual swap. `DUR-10` quotes `SEC-21` ("strip ladder rungs
  and re-sign, and thereby suppress or downgrade the `T`-time sweep"), so change the quotation in
  the same commit; the citation gate checks it.
- `SPN-38`'s "so every honest node's cumulative prefix begins at the same rung" holds only over a
  common ladder. `DUR-28`'s "quorum on an Escape's own commitment id IS cross-node agreement on
  that Escape" holds for the base; append to it rather than replace it, because
  `16-open-findings.md` quotes it.
- ADR-0016, rewritten in place: the strip-all arm (now: the base sweeps at its own fee), the
  sentence on the composer rewriting the base to `0xfffffffd`, and any ladderless-sequence
  statement; add decision 1 and the per-node split as an accepted, bounded residual.
- A new `CNF-` item: `{base, r1}`, `{base, r2}` and `{base, r3}` delivered to 2, 2 and 1 nodes on
  `n = 5`, `t = 3`; every node finalizes at the base and no rung completes.
- A new `DEF-` entry in `14-known-defects.md`, owned by `CHN-15` and `DUR-23`: the reference
  composes `0xffffffff` for a ladderless Escape and refuses a signalling base with an empty ladder
  at fire (ADR-0016 names the test `a_ladderless_escape_still_requires_a_non_signalling_sequence`).
  Not reproduced here, so not marked *verified*.
- No Lean change: `CHN-15` has no Lean declaration, and the `SPN-38` and `DUR-28` sentences are
  prose. No vector change: the commitment vector's `0xffffffff` is encoding data, not an Escape.
  No glossary change.

Out of scope: a coerced user signing the base twice with different signature bytes. It needs the
user's key, so it is not a `SEC-21` power.

**Done when** every site above is changed, the new `CNF-` and `DEF-` entries exist, a grep finds no
remaining non-signalling Escape rule, and the full gate passes unpiped with every affected
`gates.yml` step run against the working tree.

---

**Original finding (2026-10-03).**

A post-wrench coordinator can deliver different ladders over one Escape to different nodes, so no
rung reaches `t` and the sweep finalizes at the base. `SPN-38` and `DUR-28` state a cross-node
agreement that holds only for the base transaction.

**Mechanism.** `SEC-21` gives the coordinator "selectively deliver, strip ladder rungs and
re-sign". Stripping needs no user key: any non-empty subset of a signed ladder still satisfies
`CHN-16`. Each node registers the ladder it receives first. `bps-8s0.29` (decided 2026-10-03)
refuses a later different ladder as `candidate_identity`, and honest relays (`SPN-35`, `NCH-27`)
deliver every variant to every node. A rung pools partials only where `NCH-24` finds that "the
rung is found by txid".
- **Three variants, n = 5, t = 3.** Delivering `{base, r1}`, `{base, r2}` and `{base, r3}` to 2, 2
  and 1 nodes leaves every rung below `t`, so every node finalizes at rung 0. A scratch model
  confirms this (`.context/vault-review-1002/round6-ladder/split-model.lean`).
- **Two variants on n = 2t − 1 nodes.** One group has at least `t` nodes, so its ladder can still
  complete there.
- **The base.** Rung 0 is the commitment itself, and `DUR-28` walks down to it, so an admissible
  base completes. A split ladder is therefore no worse than no ladder. The base splits only if the
  user signs it twice with different signature bytes, since `NCH-24` also requires "the
  user-signature hash matches"; that needs the user's key.
- **Bound.** `SEC-21`'s "suppress or downgrade the `T`-time sweep" covers this outcome. Freeze and
  Lockdown are untouched, so this is not `DUR-34`.

**Text that overstates.**
- `SPN-38`: "so every honest node's cumulative prefix begins at the same rung" needs a common
  ladder and matching user-signature hashes.
- `DUR-28`: "quorum on an Escape's own commitment id IS cross-node agreement on that Escape" is
  true of the base transaction only. `16-open-findings.md` quotes the sentence, so append to it
  rather than replace it.
- `SEC-21` does not say that stripping differently per node is the same power.

**Owner decision wanted.** Should nodes recompute `CHN-17`'s ladder at gate 25, so the Escape's id
fixes its ladder and the rung split closes?
- Cost: `SEC-21`'s and `DOM-3`'s rung-stripping power ends, and `CHN-17` is frozen for the vault's
  life.
- Gate 25 does not stage, so that refusal grants nothing new.

Rejected already:
- Binding the ladder into `CHN-24`: partials name `commitment_id` (`NCH-23`), so a ladder split
  becomes an Escape split and not even the base completes (same scratch model).
- Merging two ladders: it mutates a resident candidate.

**Also unverified, `SPN-27`.** Does gate 25 refuse a `0xfffffffd` base with no rungs?
- `CHN-15` and `CNF-142` say that combination is invalid.
- `SPN-27` applies the ladder rules "to every rung", which checks nothing when there are none.
- `ADR-0016` says the reference "returns `Ok(())` on an empty `escape_bumps`".
- If gate 25 admits it, `DUR-23` refuses that Escape at fire time, base included.

Evidence: `.context/vault-review-1002/round6-ladder/` (brief, four answers, two scratch models).

Done when:
- the decision on recomputing `CHN-17` is recorded;
- `SPN-38`, `DUR-28` and `SEC-21` state the per-node ladder split;
- a conformance item exercises the three-variant split: the base completes and no rung does;
- the `SPN-27` empty-ladder question is answered, with a refusal row if gate 25 admits it.
close_reason: DUR-10 scope corrected in 16850d0; gates and workflow controls passed; evidence in closing comment.

title: Formal: Lockdown never blocks the in-flight Escape (DUR-7), with a planted send-latch control
description:
This bead closes the one lifecycle gap found in the 2026-10-06 review of the external proposal's
§7 (sealing, Lockdown, node death). The review declined the rest of §7: host behaviour (tmpfs,
create-only extended attributes, key erasure) or restated definitions.

## Finding

**Nothing fails if Lockdown blocks the in-flight Escape.** `DUR-7` says "Lockdown blocks NEW
signing and MUST NOT block the in-flight Escape combine the sweep needs", and `DUR-20` opens each
selected Escape's window at `T`, the same instant Lockdown lands. In the kernel, `firePass`,
`packageAccepted` and `send` do not read `Node.lockedDown`, but no theorem says so. Two reviewers
independently planted a latch check at HEAD:
- in `Kernel.firePass`: `if (r.poison == .asserted && n.poisoned) || n.lockedDown then`;
- in `Kernel.send`: `go := c.packageOk && !n.lockedDown && …`.

Each broke only proof scripts that state nothing about Lockdown (`Silence.firePass_pub`,
`Silence.send_pub`, the released-implies-exposed invariant). After one- to four-line repairs the
full gate went green. Every release theorem has the form "release implies authorized", and
blocking more releases keeps all of them true. Such an edit would send every duress event to
Recovery: `DUR-32`'s list of sweep failures does not include Lockdown, and row L7 of
`12-security-requirements.md` says "vault coins stranded after any freeze or Lockdown are
permanently lost" when recovery keys are lost. `DEF-4` records a real case where one error
"bricked arming, Lockdown and the fire path at once".

## Scope

- **`Kernel.lean`,** beside `poisoned_releases_nothing`: a theorem that `firePass`'s effects,
  `packageAccepted`'s resulting candidates and `send`'s effects are equal with `lockedDown` set
  and clear, for every rule value, environment and world. Watch out: a reviewer's first attempt,
  `⟨rfl, rfl, rfl⟩`, failed on the clean tree, so prove it properly (for example, by unfolding and
  case-splitting on the poison branch). Roughly 15 lines.
- **`gates.yml`:** one planted-mutation step, shaped like the existing ones, that adds
  `!n.lockedDown &&` to `send`'s `go`. At HEAD this plant breaks only `Silence.send_pub`. With the
  new theorem in `Kernel.lean`, the build should stop there. Measure, then pin the exact error
  count, files and declaration names, as the hint-trust step does. Measure with
  `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py '<step name>'`. Put it on a shard
  other than 3.
- **`DUR-7`** gains a "Formal scope:" paragraph, shaped like `DUR-8`'s. It names the theorem and
  its limit: it covers "MUST NOT block the in-flight Escape combine". Neither "blocks NEW
  signing" nor entering Lockdown at `T` is modelled, since the kernel sets the latch only on
  poison (`DUR-9`).

## Out of scope

- A deadline transition, whether as a new event or folded into `Kernel.tick`. `tick` is
  `NCH-40`'s prune driver, and `STO-13` gives the deadline driver its own thread. "Nothing defers
  Lockdown" is false today (`F64`, `Exhibits.TwoRun.later_commit_grows_T`).
- Admission refusal under Lockdown as a theorem. A latched node is already armed, and
  `no_hot_partial_while_armed` with `DUR-11`'s birth freeze already holds new hot spends.
- Sealing, the generation marker, reboot versus crash, and resurrection: these are host
  contracts.

## Done when

`nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0 unpiped, the new step passes under
`run-steps.py`, and every `gates.yml` step that edits `Kernel.lean` still passes with its pinned
counts (the retire, reauth, poison, defeat, traversal and dynamics flips, plus any plant an
earlier bead added).

title: CI: run the gates workflow as four parallel jobs; the identifier controls skip the kernel replay
description:
The gates workflow takes about 32 minutes on the public runner: one job, every step in series. The owner
decided on 2026-10-02 to run it as four parallel jobs and to stop the two identifier controls
from paying for a kernel replay they do not use. The design below is settled; no consultation is needed.

## Measured (2026-10-02, commit 28bae18, ubuntu-24.04 public runner, 4 CPU)

- Job: 32.5 min.
- `Run all gates`: 285 s. Inside it: dev shell 22 s, Lean build 73 s, then the index, the
  `leanchecker --fresh` replay, render and values in about 185 s, then the other eight gates in 3 s.
- The 71 controls: 1655 s in series.
- `Prove the identifier gate rejects a tag naming a withdrawn id` and `... an undefined id`:
  196 s and 193 s. Each runs the whole formal gate only to get `.lake/index.jsonl`, and the
  replay is most of that time.
- Per-step GitHub times: `/var/tmp/ctl/gh-steps-28bae18.tsv` (number, name, start, end).
- On this machine, four controls at a time peak at 11.7 GB. Each job runs its steps in series,
  so memory is not a constraint.

## 1. `tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`

- The flag skips only the `lake env leanchecker --fresh BtcPolicy` block. Everything else runs
  unchanged and in the same order: the greps, the build, the import walk, the index, render and
  values. When skipped, it prints one line saying the replay was skipped.
- Any other argument is an error that exits 2.
- `tools/check-all.sh` still calls it with no argument, so the full gate always replays.
- The two identifier controls above pass `--no-replay`. No other control changes its call: the
  other eleven expect a failure before the replay is reached.

## 2. `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: four parallel jobs

- Strategy: `fail-fast: false`, `matrix: shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]`.
- Job name: `specification gates (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})`.
- Checkout and install-nix run on every shard, with no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` gets `if: matrix.shard == 0`. Its body is unchanged.
- A new step right after it, `if: matrix.shard != 0`, runs
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check_formal.sh --no-replay`. It builds the `.lake` that the
  controls copy, including the index, regions and values that the citation, copies and regions
  controls read.
- Every control step gets exactly one `if: matrix.shard == N` in that literal form, with N in the
  matrix list. Do not reorder, rename or edit the control bodies. The two `--no-replay` edits
  are the only body changes.
- **Balance the shards from the measured times.** Shard 0 carries `Run all gates` (285 s).
  Every other shard carries the formal setup step, estimated at 130 s. Each identifier control
  is estimated at 196 s minus 150 s for the replay. Assign controls longest first (LPT) so the
  four estimated shard totals sit within 10% of their mean. Record the estimated totals in the
  report, not in the repository.

## 3. A guard that every step runs on the shards it should, with its own negative control

Write a small check (a Python script under `tools/`, run in the dev shell) and run it from a step
on shard 0. It fails, with a message naming the step, unless all of these hold:

- The matrix shard list is exactly `[0, 1, …, N-1]`.
- Checkout and install-nix have no `if:`.
- `Run all gates` has `if: matrix.shard == 0`, and its body is exactly
  `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`.
- The formal setup step has `if: matrix.shard != 0`.
- Every other step has exactly `if: matrix.shard == N`, with N in the list.
- `tools/check-all.sh` does not contain `--no-replay`.

Following this repository's rule that every gate is proven able to fail, add a control step. In a
scratch copy it deletes one control's `if:` line and asserts the guard exits nonzero with the
exact expected message. It also asserts the guard passes on the untouched copy.

## 4. Prose

Grep `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/` for any sentence that the new layout makes
false: one job, steps in order, or every step running on every push. Fix only those sentences.

- `README.md` lines 25 and 40 stay true. CI still runs `check-all.sh`, now on shard 0, and
  still breaks a document on every run.
- `AGENTS.md` keeps "`.github/workflows/gates.yml` holds the list".

No ADR is needed. This is CI layout, not a specification decision.

## Done when

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` passes, run unpiped and alone in the checkout.
- `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <steps>` passes on the working tree
  for the new guard, its control and the two identifier controls. Split the steps into chunks
  that each finish within 10 minutes.
- Each shard is replayed after the commit, in a clean worktree. That replay is the maintainer's
  job, not this one's.
- The guard's control is measured at its exact message.
- One commit. No commit message, and no added line in any file, names a model, a review tool or
  an adviser, or carries a Co-Authored-By trailer. This repository is public.
close_reason: Workflow runs as four shards; identifier controls skip the replay; tools/check_shards.py guards the layout with its own control

title: Citation gate: a word between `X` and its speech verb (`X` now says "…") leaves the quote never held to X
description:
The citation gate never holds a quote to `X` when a word stands between `` `X` `` and its speech
verb, so a false quote written "`X` now says "…"" passes.

`ATTRIB` in `tools/check_citations.py` reads `` `X` `` (or `` `X`'s ``), then optionally "own",
then the verb. Any other word between them ("now", "still", "also", "no longer", "previously")
leaves the phrase unread as an attribution. Its quote then belongs, by the gate's ownership rule, to
the last attribution starting before it in the chunk, or to no one; and an unquoted
"`X` no longer says …" is never counted.

Measured at `7f8dee2`, against `find()` in memory:
- `` `DOM-1` now says "a phrase DOM-1 has never contained anywhere". `` and the same with
  "also states" are green: nothing checked, nothing counted.
- `` `OVR-1` says "<OVR-1 text>"; `DOM-1` now says "<OVR-1 text>". `` is green: both quotes are held
  to `OVR-1`, none to `DOM-1`.
- `` `OVR-1` no longer says the rule applies. `` is green and uncounted.
- On the tree, `ADR-0023` carries `` `DUR-4` still says "Ingress never arms" ``. The quote is in
  `DUR-4`'s body today, but no check holds it there.

Not a regression: `ATTRIB` has had this shape since before `bps-2jz`. That bead removed the
history-marker exemption from the unquoted rule; its brief put `ATTRIB`'s forms out of scope. With
the exemption gone, a word between the id and the verb is the shortest way to write an attribution
the gate neither checks nor counts. The module docstring declares the README's `once said` form as
unread, but not this general shape.

Done when: the owner has decided whether a quote after "`X` <word> <verb>" is held to `X`, or the
shape is refused, or it is declared a limit in the module docstring; any quote the change newly
checks on the tree passes or is corrected; `tools/citation-baseline.json` stays byte-identical; and a
`gates.yml` case plants a false quote in the decided shape and asserts the decided result.
close_reason: The citation gate reads one KNOWN word between an id and its speech verb, leaves UNREAD unread and refuses any other word (fe6fc4c)

comments.text:
Decision, 2026-10-18: REFUSE. Between `` `X` `` and its speech verb the gate reads one word from a
known list like the bare verb, leaves the exempt words (`once`, passive auxiliaries) unread as today,
and refuses any other single word, naming `X` and the word.

Review panel, two rounds, four readers (A-D). Evidence, letter-named: round 1 in
`/var/tmp/cite-evidence/68a-panel/`, round 2 in `/var/tmp/cite-evidence/68a-panel/r2/`.
- Round 1 split 2-1-1: A and B a fixed list with every other word skipped as today (LIST); C read any

  REFUSE.
- Round 2: 4-0 for REFUSE; A, B and C changed their votes. Each reader built both options with one
  shared list (`own|now|also|still|itself|only|explicitly|currently`) and one possessive rule, so its
  two builds differ only in refusing versus skipping an unknown word.

  turns red every chunk its LIST build does; all eight builds lose the same 81 instances that are red

  identical. The reference REFUSE build below turns red 810 false instances that LIST leaves green, and
  refuses 657 genuine ones that LIST passes: an honest sentence in a shape the gate does not read gets a
  request to reword.
- On the tree at `82edf5c` every build reds only `DUR-4` in ADR-0023 and `DUR-30` in `Exhibits.lean`,

  differently is `` `CNF-47` nevertheless said `T` "never grows" `` (`16-open-findings.md` at the

  request, rest on that cost to honest prose; C and D put it as this base rate: on real writing so far

- The four REFUSE builds agree on every tree and history sentence. They differ on planted chunks in two
  details, settled by measurement:

     `` `SPN-46` then reads the coin age from the chain ``, `` requires `DUR-14` to read the resident
     register first `` and `` `WTC-11` MUST read the tip before every pass ``. This brief takes D's rule.
  2. What counts as a word: C and D `[a-z]+`; B ASCII letters in either case; A letters in any case and
     script, with internal hyphens and apostrophes. Only A's refuses every word outside the two lists
     (`` `OVR-1` Plainly says ``, `` `OVR-1` doesn't read "…" ``). This brief takes A's.
  Reference build: `r2/proto-refuse.diff` (D's REFUSE build with A's word class; gate file
  `r2/ref/refuse/tools/check_citations.py`), scored in `r2/pool-proto.out` and `r2/pool-ref.out`,
  union judge `r2/judge-proto.out`. Its module docstring still says "Any other lowercase word", which
  is false for its own word class: take the behavior from it and the prose from this brief.

Corrections to the triage comment above:
- The drafted `bps-6m5` sentence covers only spans a stray quote opens. A span that opens directly
  after an attribution is also that attribution's, and suppresses what it holds even when its closing
  mark is a later attribution's opener: `` `OVR-1`'s " `DOM-1` says "<a false phrase>" `` is green with
  nothing checked. With MIN_WORDS words or more in such a span the chunk goes red naming `OVR-1`, as
  for a stray span. The brief carries the corrected sentence, checked on six probes under every build
  (`r2/probes.py`, `r2/probes.out`).
- The tree has a fifth sentence of this shape, `` `DUR-22`'s alone, which states: "…" `` in
  `17-operator-program.md`; two words stand between, so it stays unread (a declared limit below).

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Between `` `X` `` and its speech verb the citation gate reads one word from a known list
like the bare verb, leaves the exempt words (`once`, passive auxiliaries) unread as today, and refuses
any other single word or `no longer` after `` `X` ``, naming `X` and the word. Two exceptions: an
unknown word before an unquoted `reads`/`read` is a consult, which the gate reads past, and after

**Current behavior:**
`ATTRIB` in `tools/check_citations.py` reads `` `X` `` or `` `X`'s ``, optionally `own`, then a verb

attribution before it in the chunk or to no one, and an unquoted claim is never counted. Both
`` `OVR-1` also says "<a false phrase>" `` and `` `OVR-1` no longer says the rule applies `` are

title: A routine rotation that keeps the PINs puts fresh digests of them on the coordinator while the predecessor still holds the coins, and no destroy step reaches them in time
description:
Type: bug. Proposed priority: P2 (the same failure as `bps-363`: the silence claim does not hold
against the adversary it names, here during a routine rotation that keeps the PINs; the window is
bounded but unavoidable once the PINs are reused). Kind: requirement and Operator procedure. Found
by the post-Run counterexample-trace review of `bps-363` at `c4d5a17`.

**Example.** Vault 1 is funded. A node patch triggers a routine rotation, and the user keeps the
same two PINs. Vault 2's ceremony runs on the coordinator, so fresh digests of those PINs sit there
from `assemble` until vault 2's last node start. Vault 1 still holds the coins through all of that.
A wrench comes in that window. Whoever holds the coordinator tests each PIN the user enters against
vault 2's digests, drops the duress request, and demands the other PIN.

**Why no rule covers it** (all at `c4d5a17`)

- The destruction deadline is per vault. `OPS-35`: "After the last node start (`MAN-36`) and before
  the vault is first funded (`OPS-36`), the Operator MUST destroy every copy of either PIN digest
  that is not on a node host". Vault 1's deadline passed long ago; vault 2's cannot arrive before
  vault 2's last node start, and the copies must exist until then.
- The ceremony runs on the coordinator: `MAN-24`'s table has "the coordinator | `assemble`" and
  "the coordinator | `finalize`".
- A routine rotation builds the successor while the predecessor is funded. `OPS-30`: "a rotation
  triggered by a **patch, a dead node, a planned key change, a forgotten PIN or a lost recovery
  key** verifies the successor FIRST (`OPS-59` step 1) and sweeps only once a valid successor
  exists". `OPS-59`: "(1) create and VERIFY a successor vault — a fresh ceremony whose output is
  checked against the predecessor's" comes before "(2) move the funds by a claw-back through the
  Normal path".
- Reusing the PINs is allowed. `OPS-30`: "For a compromise-signal rotation, the Operator SHOULD
  enroll successor PINs such that neither new PIN verifies against either predecessor digest,
  including when the PIN roles are swapped." and "This recommendation does not apply to routine
  rotations."
- The premise reads two ways, and both leave a gap.
  - `SEC-10`'s other premise is about the PINs over their lifetime: "Its **release-history
    premise** is that no node has run a compromised release while the current PINs were in use."
    The new one is about digests: "Its **digest premise** is that the adversary holds no copy of
    either PIN digest."
  - Strictly, vault 2's digests are not copies of vault 1's (each has its own salt), so the premise
    holds and `DUR-1` still claims silence: "Silence is claimed against an adversary holding the
    coordinator and the physical scene but no node, subject to `SEC-10`'s "release-history
    premise" and "digest premise"". The coordinator's holder can nonetheless test every PIN.
  - Loosely, as `OPS-35` itself reads "copy" when it lists "any copy left from an earlier vault
    whose PINs are reused", the premise fails and the claim is honestly scoped, but no destroy
    step removes the copy while vault 1 is at risk.
- A rollout stage's two vaults can open the same window. `OPS-38`: the **Survivor** "stays funded
  and running". `OPS-34` forbids sharing only recovery keys: "The two vaults of a rollout stage
  MUST NOT share recovery keys, because the Sacrificial vault's ceremony deliberately exposes and
  uses them." If one vault's ceremony runs while the other is funded and they share PINs, the
  funded vault is exposed in the same way.

**Fix direction: open, technical, for the panel at triage.** Two candidates, neither chosen:

1. New PINs on every rotation (and for a stage's second vault), so no other vault's ceremony ever
   holds a digest of a funded vault's PIN.
2. A scope sentence for the window: the digest premise reads as a digest of either current PIN in
   any vault, and the claim names the period in which another vault's ceremony holds one.

Out of scope: a compromise-signal rotation sweeps first ("sweeps FIRST and builds the successor
after", `OPS-30`), so its predecessor holds no coins during the successor's ceremony.

**A separate inference, not checked by any reading round.** A copy that destruction cannot reach
(`SEC-10`: "Destruction cannot revoke a copy already taken") may also allow an offline PIN guess
by someone who does not hold the PIN. The set fixes no PIN format (`MAN-20`), and `MAN-21` sets only
ceilings on the Argon2 cost ("`m > 262 144` KiB, `t > 10`, or `p > 16`"), with no floor. `SEC-26`
says "Higher-entropy PINs are defence in depth, not load-bearing". If a thief holding only the user
key also holds such a copy and recovers the normal PIN by search, `SEC-54` row 1's "Nothing"
(`SPN-18`: "no PIN, no valid request") would overstate; the row-2 outcome, Bounded, would apply.
The `SEC-54` preamble's digest sentence covers only a coercer: "A coercer who holds one anyway can
test the PIN offered before relaying it and withhold a duress request". This predates `bps-363`
and is recorded for triage, not decided here.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug

**Summary:** Every rotation enrolls new PINs, neither verifying against a predecessor digest nor
enrolled in any other vault, in either role (`OPS-30`), and a rollout stage's two vaults share no
PIN with each other or with any other vault (`OPS-34`), as Operator duties enrollment tooling does not check; `SEC-10`'s "digest premise"
includes that neither PIN is enrolled in another vault and says why; `DUR-1`, the `SEC-54`
preamble, `CONTEXT.md`, the executive summary, the `BtcPolicy.Silence` docstring and `CNF-130`
carry it; `ADR-0021` records the change to its 2026-10-05 decision and names the narrowing of
`ADR-0012`'s "Silence model A", which stays unedited.

**Current behavior:**
`OPS-30` makes new PINs a recommendation for a compromise-signal rotation only: "This
recommendation does not apply to routine rotations." A routine rotation "verifies the successor
FIRST", so a user who keeps the PINs has them enrolled in two vaults while the predecessor holds
coins, and after the sweep `OPR-66` says "Retirement MUST preserve the locally held artifacts and
signing access". Whoever holds the coordinator at the wrench can then test each PIN the user enters
against the other vault: through its digests while they exist, and against its running nodes with
its coordinator auth key, without coins. `DUR-1` still claims silence against that adversary.
`OPS-34` lets a stage's two vaults share PINs with each other, and with an earlier stage's
Survivor, which "stays funded and running" (`OPS-38`). The description and the review above have the
evidence.

**Desired behavior:** these eleven edits, as written.

1. `OPS-30`, replacing "For a compromise-signal rotation, the Operator SHOULD enroll successor PINs such that neither new PIN verifies against either predecessor digest, including when the PIN roles are swapped. Enrollment tooling does not check this recommendation; it adds no ceremony refusal, digest comparison or predecessor-digest persistence, and the rotation does not require the old PINs. This recommendation does not apply to routine rotations." with: "For every rotation, the Operator MUST enroll successor PINs such that neither new PIN verifies against either predecessor digest, including when the PIN roles are swapped, and neither is enrolled in any other vault, in either role. Enrollment tooling does not check this duty; it adds no ceremony refusal, digest comparison or predecessor-digest persistence, and the rotation does not require the old PINs. A PIN enrolled in another vault leaves `SEC-10`'s "digest premise" unmet."

2. `OPS-34`, replacing "**OPS-34** The two vaults of a rollout stage MUST NOT share recovery keys, because the Sacrificial vault's ceremony deliberately exposes and uses them." with: "**OPS-34** The two vaults of a rollout stage MUST NOT share recovery keys, because the Sacrificial vault's ceremony deliberately exposes and uses them. They MUST NOT share either PIN, in either role, with each other or with any other vault, because a PIN enrolled in two vaults can be tested in either while the other holds coins (`SEC-10`); enrollment tooling does not check this."

3. `SEC-10`, replacing "premise** is that the adversary holds no copy of either PIN digest. `OPS-35` requires every copy off the node hosts to be destroyed before funding; that procedure does not establish the premise, and no theorem does." with: "premise** is that the adversary holds no copy of either PIN digest and that neither PIN is enrolled in another vault, in either role. A digest of a PIN enrolled in another vault is such a copy, whatever its salt, since `OPS-35` says "each digest checks a PIN against its enrolled role in one Argon2 evaluation"; and whoever holds that vault's coordinator auth key, a coordinator serving both vaults included, can test the PIN against that vault's running nodes without coins: a request carrying a PIN not enrolled there is refused `BAD_PIN` (`SPN-18`) before any coin is fetched (`SPN-5`), and a staged one carrying that vault's duress PIN, accepted or refused, arms it once its holder set reaches `t` (`DUR-4`, `DUR-5`), so it locks down at `T` (`DUR-7`). `OPS-30` forbids such enrolment for a rotation's successor and `OPS-34` for a rollout stage's vaults, and `OPS-35` requires every copy off the node hosts to be destroyed before funding; these procedures do not establish the premise, and no theorem does."

11. `ADR-0021`, a dated decision appended after "Decision 2026-10-21: the fund outcome of row 16":

## Decision 2026-10-21: new PINs

Accepted: every rotation needs new PINs. `OPS-30` says "the Operator MUST enroll successor PINs such
that neither new PIN verifies against either predecessor digest", including role swaps, and neither
enrolled in any other vault; `OPS-34` says a rollout stage's two vaults "MUST NOT share either PIN,
in either role, with each other or with any other vault". Both are Operator duties that enrollment
tooling does not check, as `OPS-35`'s destruction of digest copies is. This changes the decision of
2026-10-05 on compromised releases and predecessor data, whose recommendation was deliberately
advisory and did not apply to routine rotations. Where a PIN is also enrolled in another vault,
whoever holds that vault's coordinator auth key can test it against that vault's running nodes
without coins (`SEC-10`), and `OPR-66` says "Retirement MUST preserve the locally held artifacts and
signing access", so the coordinator keeps a predecessor's key after the sweep, and no rule stops the
predecessor's nodes. `SEC-10`'s "digest premise" now includes that neither PIN is enrolled in
another vault. This decision narrows the current application of `ADR-0012`'s unnumbered "Silence
model A" threat-model bullet a third time: silence is not claimed where either PIN is enrolled in
another vault, against any adversary, even one "who has compromised **no node**". `ADR-0012`
remains unchanged as the historical design record.

Rejected: a recommendation that lets the user reuse a PIN, which leaves silence unclaimed against
the coordinator itself while the other vault's nodes run; and allowing reuse once the other
vault's nodes are stopped or its coordinator auth key deleted, which conflicts with `OPR-66`'s
retention and `OPS-15`'s claw-back route.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] `OPS-30` and `OPS-34` state the duty as a MUST that enrollment tooling does not check, and
      `OPS-30` keeps "the rotation does not require the old PINs" (edits 1, 2).
- [ ] `SEC-10`'s "digest premise" includes that neither PIN is enrolled in another vault, with the

title: Citation gate never checks a quotation longer than 400 characters; two WTC-14 quotations in Watchtower.lean go unread
description:
The citation gate never checks a quotation longer than 400 characters, and stays green when one is
wrong.

`QUOTE` in `tools/check_citations.py` pairs quotes only for spans of 8 to 400 characters. A longer
quotation is no span: its text is read as prose, and nothing compares it with its owner's body.

Measured at `4ddca43`: `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Watchtower.lean` carries two `WTC-14` colon-form
quotations, "A pass whose tip is below the newest anchor MUST return without advancing; … resets the
cursor to genesis", of 497 and 496 characters. Neither is checked, and the verified count does not
include them. Their words inside read as prose: before `bps-mmt` the "no longer" in them exempted both
chunks as history.

Done when: a quotation over the cap is either checked whole or refused (the choice is the owner's;
splitting into shorter quotes with `…` is one remedy the gate already supports); every quotation
the change newly checks passes or is corrected; and a `gates.yml` negative control corrupts one word
inside a quotation longer than 400 characters and asserts the refusal.
close_reason: Landed at 9a9a9d5; follow-ups bps-ll0, bps-6m5

comments.text:
Decision, 2026-10-15, the owner's: shape S, check a long quotation whole. Reached through a
four-reviewer review in two rounds (briefs, answers and prototypes in `/var/tmp/cite-evidence/`:
`brief-r1.md`, `r1-<reviewer>.md` Question B, `brief-r2.md`, `r2-<reviewer>.md`; the S prototype is
`S-build.diff`, built at `1e1fadd`, before `bps-uwy` and `bps-2jz` landed). Round 1 split four ways.
A plain lift of the cap was ruled out: a stray straight quote (`6"`) more than 400 characters before
`` `OVR-1` reads "<false>" `` takes the quotation's opener, the attribution then owns no quote, and
`reads` with no quote is a consult, so the false quote is green. Round 2: all four chose S over
refusing long quotations (R) and over keeping the cap with an uncapped match at direct openers only
(O).

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** The citation gate checks a quotation of any length, and pairing restarts at the explicit
opener after every attribution, so a stray quote mark before an attribution cannot swallow its
quotation.

**Current behavior:** `QUOTE` pairs only spans of 8 to 400 characters. Three attributed quotations
are longer (two `WTC-14` in `Watchtower.lean`, one `WTC-24` in `Package.lean`) and are never
checked, so a wrong word inside them is green. Two further shapes are green at today's cap, verified
at `1e1fadd` against the S prototype: `` `OVR-1` reads "<false phrase plus about 450 characters>" ``
(no span, so `reads` is a consult), and `` A 6" field and the node reads it, and `OVR-1` reads "<false>" ``
(the near stray mark takes the opener). `ANCHORED_QUOTE`'s re-scan repairs pairing only after a
direct opener (colon or possessive).

**Desired behavior:** `QUOTE` has no upper length bound. Every attribution outside a quotation an
earlier attribution introduced restarts pairing at its explicit opener, as direct openers do today,
so a quote mark before it cannot pair across it. All three shapes above go red naming `OVR-1`, and
the three long quotations in the tree are checked and pass. The known cost, accepted: a stray quote
mark after an attribution and far from its quotation can pair with that quotation's opener and fail
the chunk blaming the prose between; that is a red, never a green.

**Key interfaces:** `QUOTE`, `ANCHORED_QUOTE` and the pairing repair in `find()`; the module docstring,
which must state the new pairing, drop every statement of the 400-character limit, and state the
accepted false red.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] No length bound on a quotation; the three long quotations are checked (the verified count rises
      by three on an otherwise unchanged tree) and pass.
- [ ] The three shapes in "Current behavior" fail the gate naming `OVR-1`, each as a `gates.yml` case.
- [ ] A `gates.yml` negative control corrupts one word past character 400 inside an existing long
      quotation (the `WTC-14` one), with straight and with curly delimiters, and asserts exit 1, the
      owner's diagnostic line, and the baseline bytes unchanged.
- [ ] Every existing citation case still passes, or its changed expectation is named in the closing
      comment with the reason.
- [ ] `tools/citation-baseline.json` byte-identical; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`
      exits 0, run unpiped.

**Out of scope:** quotations that run past a sentence end (`bps-` follow-up filed with this decision);
the teaching phrases (`bps-mxm`); a word between an id and its speech verb (`bps-68a`); the quoted and
unquoted rules otherwise.
