title: Milestone 7: selected Escapes, accounting bridge, SILENCE as a two-run relation
description: ADR-0023 decision 10 item 7. Selected set: List (EscapeId × Bool) keyed by Escape commitment id with DUR-10's OR-merge; a normal-PIN entry never released whatever sweepActive does (F54 fix row 4); every holder decision and hot acceptance writes every window (DUR-20) as a writes count equal under both PINs. DUR-22 denominator computed from ChainView + the selected set with restoreAll; theorem it is the same value on every pass while the set only grows; distinguish equality across candidates in one environment, preservation across the sequence, agreement across nodes — if the across-pass claim needs more than DUR-22's construction supplies, return the precise gap to DUR-22 as a finding (first reader §4). Accounting bridge: POL-18/POL-19 reserve/refund/age-out transitions establish milestone 3's counting premises for POL-20's cohort; ADR-0014's trace becomes a reachable exhibit and the withdrawn completion bound a refuted theorem (¬ ∀ window, completed <= n/t × cap) while the admission theorem holds; SPN-33 mempool settlement refunds nothing. SILENCE: Obs structure (response shape, /pending, /healthz bucket, /events queue, peer message shapes and sizes, abstract work counts) with observe ∘ step = stepObs ∘ observe on every prefix where now < current T (DUR-14 dynamic, may be zero, sticky once ended); two worlds = one request body with two enrolments (SEC-10); leaky twins: DEF-12's arm-conditioned marker and F54's conditional window traversal; docstring says counts are not durations (F22, SEC-47). F3, F4, F13 kept as traces with no repair chosen. Glossary gains observer projection and concealment horizon when this lands.
notes:
Q1 DECIDED 2026-09-19 (four-reader panel, .context/m7-q1b-*.md; landed as F59 + amendments to DUR-22/24/28/31, CNF-140, MAN-9, ADR-0020, commit e74d9ff): Coverage denominator = filter on the chain read + every distinct selected input outpoint added once (counted regardless of the read; precedence over exclusions) — NOT confirmed+restored-excluded; rebuild Coverage.denominator from a ChainView + selected set. Theorems: (i) one value per pass; (ii) floor: P >= union of selected inputs on every pass; (iii) per-node single sweep under "both selected at this node's first release"; (iv) aggregate burn <= (100-pct)% of swept. Exhibits kept: restoreOne (F54), unconfirmed-external-deposit two-pass trace, subtracting-shape breaks the floor, cross-node 2-of-3 trace, late-selection trace, phantom-prevout denial. No snapshot, no ingress rule.

Q2 DECIDED 2026-09-20 (three-reader panel, .context/m7-q2-*.md; the clock gap landed as F60). SILENCE relation: one request body, two enrolments (NOT two PIN bodies; CNF-40 is the conformance approximation). Horizon = the duress run's CURRENT T (DUR-13 then DUR-14 shrinks), guard on the state ENTERING each step so the arming receipt is always inside the prefix (its effects are the last shared observable, and DEF-12's twin sits there); sticky by prefix quantification, since Effective is not monotone. Freeze-invisible is a LIVE INVARIANT over the holder-decision scan, not an unconditional inequality, and carries a non-decreasing-sample hypothesis (F60). Obs carries response BYTES/refusal codes, Effect.broadcast, /healthz locked_down + last_deadline_tick, ordered peer effects with destinations and sizes — not shapes and aggregate counts; omits timing class, allocations, lock-hold time (F22/SEC-47). Theorem shape = coupling invariant between the two runs with equal observable effects per step, NOT observe-commutes-with-step. Twins: (a) DEF-12 arm-keyed marker, (b) F54 conditional window traversal, (c) static T — FAITHFUL, ADR-0012's 2026-07-15 log says "One true silence break -> FIXED: dynamic T", so a real guard parameter; plus a fourth NEGATIVE EXHIBIT (not a flip): duress-only selected-entry insertion, which also opens SPN-41's capacity probe. One node; the federation horizon is the first node's crossing, a corollary, and no federation claim is made.

Q3 DECIDED 2026-09-20 (three-reader panel, .context/m7-q3-*.md; landed as F61 CLOSED + F62 OPEN + POL-20 and DOM-24 amended). Accounting bridge = a ledger transition model (reserve at acceptance POL-18/SPN-29, refund only at terminal-without-exposure POL-18/SPN-33, one-way age-out POL-19) COMPOSED WITH milestone 4's kernel — a ledger-only model cannot make ADR-0014's trace reachable (needs holder decisions, releases, settlement, completion). Bookkeeping: Ledgers.counting has TWO hypotheses (hcap, hq), not three; hq already fuses "at least t-c acceptances" with "still charged at the cut", so H2/H3 are bridge lemmas, not arguments. No-age-out lemma: TRUE, needs only that the reservation is in the trailing interval; POL-17 not needed; saturating Nat subtraction truncates toward live; requires non-decreasing HotClock samples in the trace (Kernel.Reachable admits arbitrary Env samples today — add the premise). Cohort exclusion is PER RESERVATION; per spend the conclusion is false. H1 needs the one-way-release model (F62). A1 also needs a reservation map keyed by commitment id with the authoritative amount, and a well-formed cohort (distinct ids, amounts matching) or Ledgers.charge's hcap cannot be derived. ADR-0014 refutation is EXISTENTIAL over a reachable trace (exists start, completed in [start, start+W) > (n/t) x cap), not a bare forall-negation; the trace hits exactly 2V so it refutes the n/t reading and NOT the loss-div-t sizing rule. New twin required by decision 6: DEF-5 / F57's settlement-refund row (current retains on mempool-only settlement per SPN-33, withdrawn refunds on any settlement), distinct from milestone 4's pending-log flag. The ledger is NOT in Obs but IS part of Q2's two-run relational invariant (later HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED and work counts are observable); DUR-11 keeps the freeze off it, POL-21 puts the frozen candidate's refund strictly after Lockdown, past the horizon.
close_reason: Milestone 7 complete: the Armed overlay, the coverage denominator, the Hot ledger and accounting bridge, and SILENCE as a two-run relation, with F59-F64 recorded along the way

title: M7.1 Armed overlay on the kernel: T, sweep_active, selected set, DUR-14 shrink + DUR-20 traversal, monotone-sample premise
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 1 — the Armed overlay on milestone 4's kernel. BLOCKS 7.2, 7.3, 7.4: neither
the bridge nor the SILENCE relation can be stated against the kernel as it stands.

Extend `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Kernel.lean` (its docstring's scope cut names exactly this work):

- Overlay on `Node`: `T` (wall domain — DUR-13 computes it from `first_seen`, an effective time,
  and `earliest_hot`, a `fireAt : Wall`; it is compared against the effective sample, so add the
  named comparison to `Clocks.lean`, never a raw field read), `sweepActive : Bool`, and
  `selected : List (EscapeId × Bool)` with DUR-10's OR-merge. DUR-10: `active` "has exactly one
  writer — the holder decision with `arm = true` — and once set it is never cleared".
- Holder decision (already one step, DUR-5): additionally insert the intent's Escape id with its
  duress bit OR-merged, compute `T` per DUR-13 (`Deadline.initialT` is the arithmetic), install
  every selected Escape's fire window `[T, T + combine_slack_secs]` (DUR-20; SPN-37 registers the
  Escape with none), and set `sweepActive` on a duress commit. Pin-uniform: DUR-5's "identical
  scan, overlay write, set insertion and window refresh", differing only in one internal bit.
- Hot acceptance while armed: DUR-14's shrink (`Deadline.shrink`), and re-install EVERY selected
  window unconditionally — DUR-20: "an actual shrink MUST NOT trigger a traversal a non-shrink
  does not". The traversal count must not depend on whether `T` moved.
- Release gating per entry: `sweepActive` AND the entry's own duress bit (DUR-10), so a normal-PIN
  entry is never released (F54's row).
- `Reachable` gains a non-decreasing-sample premise on the trace — it admits arbitrary `Env`
  samples today, and both F60 (effective) and the ledger's no-age-out lemma (mono) need it.
  State it as a hypothesis on the trace, not as a clock-type property: `Effective` is not
  monotone, since the high-water advances on an accept only (SPN-13).

Every milestone-4 theorem stays green, and the four CI flips stay red at their measured counts.
Done when `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green and each existing flip is
re-measured locally. One commit + beads close.

Rebuild `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Coverage.lean`: `denominator` today takes `vaultAsArmed` as a

one selected Escape spends another's change output (CHN-30 permits vault change). Build it
instead from a `ChainView` and the selected set as a SET construction: filter the live read by
the exclusions (selected-Escape and resident-rung outputs), then union in each distinct selected
input outpoint ONCE at its `witness_utxo` value, counted whatever the read says of it; counted
inputs take precedence over every exclusion. Never subtract after unioning.

Theorems:
- Within one pass every selected Escape is measured against the same value.
- The floor: on every pass the denominator is at least the union of the selected Escapes' inputs.
- Per-node single sweep: two input-disjoint Escapes both selected at this node's first release
  cannot both cover, whatever moved the denominator between their passes.
- Aggregate burn: this node's total sweep burn is at most `100 − escape_coverage_pct` percent of
  what it sweeps, which is also what makes DUR-24's own fee-cap sentence true.

Exhibits (keep the existing `restoreOne` twin, F54): the unconfirmed-external-deposit two-pass
trace; the subtracting shape breaking the floor; the cross-node 2-of-3 trace where two honest
nodes selected different Escapes and both confirm; the late-selection trace; the phantom-prevout
denial. The last three are residuals F59 records, not defects to repair here.

Selected-set semantics from 7.1: release requires `sweepActive` AND the entry's own bit, so a
normal-PIN entry is never released. Tags DUR-22, DUR-24, DUR-10, MAN-9 at clause granularity.
Done when check-all is green. One commit + beads close.

title: M7.3 Ledger.lean + the accounting bridge: one-way age-out, hcap/hq for POL-20's node-indexed cohort, ADR-0014 reachable, DEF-5 twin
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 3 — the Hot ledger and the accounting bridge (Q3, panel
.context/m7-q3-*.md; F61, F62; POL-20 as amended). Depends on 7.1.

New `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Ledger.lean`: a reservation map keyed by commitment id holding the
authoritative amount, the reservation time, the expiry and the exposure bit (SPN-33 keeps all
four independently of candidate residency). Transitions: reserve at acceptance with POL-16's
admission check and POL-18's idempotent retry ("a retry keeps the original reservation time");
refund ONLY at a terminal state reached without exposure, and never on mempool-only settlement
(SPN-33); age-out as a ONE-WAY release, POL-19's predicate being the condition for releasing
rather than a membership test re-run (F62 — re-running it lets a backward wall step resurrect a
reclaimed charge and put the live sum over the cap).

Bridge to `Ledgers.counting`, which has TWO hypotheses, `hcap` and `hq`, not three: `hq` already
fuses "at least `t − c` acceptances" with "still charged at the cut".
- `hcap` from the live-sum invariant, by induction over the transitions (needs the one-way
  release above). SPN-29's registration-refused reservation is unwound in the same step, so the
  intermediate state is not reachable; the 4 096-entry refusal inserts nothing.
- `hq` from POL-20's node-indexed cohort plus the no-age-out lemma: a reservation whose time lies
  in that node's trailing `hot_window_secs` at the cut is still live there. The lemma needs only
  membership in the trailing interval — POL-17 is NOT needed, saturating `Nat` subtraction
  truncates toward live, and the boundaries are inclusive — plus 7.1's non-decreasing Mono
  samples, without which a charge can be released at one sample and be live again at a later one.
- Well-formedness the bridge needs and `Ledgers.charge` does not assume: distinct commitment ids,
  each cohort amount equal to the stored amount, distinct honest ledgers.
- The cohort counts only reservations not refunded while unexposed, PER RESERVATION: per spend the
  counting theorem's conclusion is false, not merely unproved (F61).

ADR-0014 reachable: compose the ledger with 7.1's kernel — a ledger-only model cannot reach it,
since the trace needs holder decisions, releases, settlement and completion. State the refutation
existentially over that trace: some window of length `hot_window_secs` completes more than
`(n / t) × cap`. It hits exactly `2V`, so it refutes the `n / t` reading and NOT the
`loss ÷ t` sizing rule; say so, and keep the admission theorem standing beside it.

New guard parameter (ADR-0023 decision 6 requires it — F57's DEF-5 row is a dated repair):
settlement refunds, `retainOnMempool` current versus `refundOnAnySettlement` withdrawn, red in
`Exhibits.lean` only, the exhibit showing the premature refund admitting another spend while the
first's exposed authority is still usable. Distinct from milestone 4's pending-log flag.

POL-21: the freeze does not touch the ledger, and a frozen candidate's refund waits for the
expiry sweep strictly after Lockdown. Tags POL-16, POL-18, POL-19, POL-20, POL-21, SPN-33.
Done when check-all is green and the new flip is measured red locally. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: done

title: M7.4 Silence.lean: Obs, two-run coupling invariant, entering-state horizon, three twins + one exhibit, glossary terms
description:
Milestone 7, ticket 4 — SILENCE as a two-run relation (Q2, panel .context/m7-q2-*.md; F60).
Depends on 7.1. Best done after 7.3, since the ledger is part of the relational invariant.

New `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Silence.lean`.

`Obs`: response BYTES and refusal codes (DUR-1 says "response bytes", and a refusal code is every
capacity and budget twin's channel), the pending projection, /healthz's bucket plus `locked_down`
and `last_deadline_tick` (API-19), the /events queue, `Effect.broadcast`, and ordered peer effects
with destinations, shapes and sizes — an ordered trace, not aggregate counts. Omit, and say so in
the docstring: timing class, allocation counts, store-lock hold time. Counts are not durations
(F22, SEC-47: "End-to-end timing has no hard gate"), and a unit-cost model must not be advertised
as constant-time.

Two worlds: ONE request body with two enrolments, the enrolment table being the secret. Not two
PIN bodies — the coordinator knows what it sent, so two bodies differ in a public input. CNF-40's
"identical under both PINs" is the conformance experiment that approximates this, not its
statement.

The relation is a COUPLING INVARIANT between the two runs with equal observable effects at each
step, not `observe ∘ step = stepObs ∘ observe`: identical observations do not determine the next
output, and exposing hidden fields to make a projection commute would defeat the purpose.

The horizon is a guard on the state ENTERING each step: unarmed, or the effective sample below
that state's current `T`. So the arming receipt is always inside the prefix and its own effects
are the last shared observable, which is where DEF-12's twin lives. Sticky by prefix
quantification, because `Effective` is not monotone. The horizon may be zero (DUR-14: "a hot
spend whose Hold already matured at arm time collapses the window to now").

Freeze-invisible is a LIVE INVARIANT over DUR-13's holder-decision scan, carrying 7.1's
non-decreasing-sample premise: without it a matured hot spend is due under normal and frozen
under duress at a sample still below `T` (F60, the retained trace).

Twins, guard parameters red in `Exhibits.lean` only: DEF-12's marker keyed on the arm bit instead
of the pin-uniform `committed`; F54's conditional window traversal; and static `T` — faithful,
ADR-0012's 2026-07-15 log records "One true silence break → FIXED: dynamic T". Plus ONE negative
exhibit that is not a flip: a duress-only selected-entry insertion, which also opens SPN-41's
capacity probe.

The ledger (7.3) is not in `Obs` but is part of the relational invariant: a duress-only refund
surfaces later as a HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED and in the work counts.

Scope: one node. DUR-1 is per node ("Every observable a node emits"); peers' relays are inputs
held equal, and the federation horizon is the first node's crossing, stated as a corollary by
events with no federation claim made. Docstring names what is not claimed: machine timing, a
compromised node or pre-wrench coordinator (SEC-10), any Lockdown latency (DUR-15, F13, SEC-48),
the cover story's plausibility, and anything past `T`. F3, F4, F13 and F60 stay traces with no
repair chosen.

CONTEXT.md gains **observer projection** and **concealment horizon** when this lands (ADR-0023
decision 7: the terms enter the glossary when the first model uses them). Done when check-all is
green and all three flips are measured red locally. One commit + beads close.
close_reason: SILENCE as a two-run relation landed: Silence.lean with the coupling invariant, the entering-state horizon, the three twins and the non-flip exhibit; F64 recorded

description: ADR-0023 decision 10 item 3; pulled ahead of the encoders by both panel readers. title: Review fixes for bps-sio, bps-mmt, bps-pxp.1 and bps-pxp.2: false sentences, weak checks, second homes
description:
Review fixes for `bps-sio`, `bps-mmt`, `bps-pxp.1` and `bps-pxp.2` (two-axis review of
`e50abc5..2609756`, 2026-10-12). No decision changes: each item is a false sentence, a weaker check
than the ticket asked for, or a second home of a rule. Verify each item against the tree before
changing it — the line references are from the review, not guarantees.

## False statements

1. `tools/check_formal.sh`: the comment says a declaration list "left by an earlier run is never
   read stale", but the `rm -f` sits after the script's early exits, so a failing local run leaves
   the old list for `check_citations.py`. Move the removal to the top.
2. `tools/check_citations.py` `read_index()`: "Shared with check_regions.py and check_ids.py -- one
   reader, not three" and its missing-file message no longer describe who reads the index
   (`check_citations.py` no longer does; `check_copies.py` imports it). Make both true.
3. `tools/check_citations.py` `HISTORICAL` comment (and `bps-mmt`'s closing comment): "each stem's
   forms spelled out" is false — only `withdraw` has its forms, and "withdrawing" no longer
   matches. Fix the regex or the comment.
4. `ADR-0028`: "The owner accepted that residual with the first ticket" — `bps-pxp.1` stated the
   backward-step residual under its *Formal* section and left it unfixed; the owner did not rule on
   it. Say that, and name `bps-pxp.1` / `bps-pxp.2` instead of "first ticket" / "two tickets".
5. `MAN-29`: the ceremony's floor sentence drops `SEC-37`'s "except through such a spend". Quote or
   cite it whole.
6. `CNF-47`: check "the earliest such record lowers `T`" against a trace where `T` was already
   lowered since the arm (reviewer B: 640, not 650); `CNF-47` is test guidance, so an
   implementation's suite would assert the wrong value. `bps-pxp.2` reports fixing ticket 1's gaps
   (1) and (2) — confirm, and fix what remains.
7. Unquoted claims about `DUR-13`: `SPN-41`'s "starts at a seed `max(ratchet, now)` (`DUR-13`)",
   the `Clocks.Effective.deadlineReached` docstring. Quote `DUR-13` or cite it without claiming.

## Checks weaker than asked

8. `BtcPolicy.Exhibits…backward_step_keeps_duress_start`: its docstring says 1200 is "not reached by
   `DUR-7`'s driver at the ratchet"; the theorem asserts only `armed` and `T = 1200`. Assert
   `deadlineReached … = false` (its withdrawn twin asserts `= true`).
9. `Kernel.HotDomain` carries two choices in one guard (which candidates are in the domain; a repeat
   reads the resident). `AGENTS.md`: every semantic choice is a guard parameter — split it, each
   with its own flip control asserting errors in `Exhibits.lean` only, counts measured.
10. `.github/workflows/gates.yml`: the `$((before + 4))` expectation in the citation-gate step is
   hand-derived from the planted string; derive it from the plant or assert the names directly.

## One rule, one home

11. What the declaration list holds is restated in about nine places (`CONTEXT.md` *Declaration
    list*, `ADR-0023` decision 1 and its rejected option, `README.md`'s `check_formal.sh` row,
    `check_formal.sh`, `Exe.lean` twice, `check_citations.py`'s NAMES docstring, `LEAN` comment and
    `lean_names`). Keep `ADR-0023` decision 1 as the home; point at it elsewhere. `Req.lean`'s
    docstring and `ADR-0023`'s *Consequences* restate `check-all.sh`'s reader list (the ADR copy
    omits `check_ids.py`): cite the list.
12. How to quote genuinely withdrawn wording lives only in `check_citations.py`'s docstring.
    `README.md` *Requirement conventions* owns retention ("Withdrawn wording is retained only where a
    trap sits behind it"): add the how there, point the docstring and the gate's failure hint at
    it, and drop the docstring's copied numbers ("eight characters", "four or more words").
13. `CONTEXT.md`: *Arm intent* restates `DUR-13`'s rule, *Hot domain* carries mechanism ("On a
    repeat, `DUR-14` reads the resident"), *Declaration list* cites no owner. Terms only, owner
    cited. "seed" is listed under *Preimage*'s `_Avoid_`; give `DUR-13`'s seed a flagged-ambiguity
    line or another word.
14. `SEC-37`'s "caps `T` at the value it had while live … no route" argument appears in `SEC-37` and
    twice in `ADR-0028`; `ADR-0028` *Consequences* copies a `DUR-13` sentence unquoted; `CNF-47`
    restates the domain. One home each; quote elsewhere.

## Stop rule

Accept when items 1–14 are done and the gate is green unpiped. A Panel finding outside this list goes
into the closing comment, not a new Round, unless it shows a sentence of a requirement stating false
behaviour.

Two of four Panel reviewers timed out; the two that answered had no findings. Details and the notes left outside the list are in the closing comment.

title: `SEC-54` row 9 fits a wrench that begins mid-spend and says Lockdown follows; `SEC-42` says no node locks down
description:
Type: bug. Proposed priority: P3. Kind: requirement text. No behaviour change.

`SEC-42` counts a wrench that begins mid-spend among the histories that nullify duress. Row 8 cites
`SEC-42`, and its outcome agrees. `SEC-54` says "This matrix names the outcome for every combination
of what the attacker holds and what the Operator still holds". Read that way, by what the attacker
holds, row 9 fits this history too, and row 9 says Lockdown follows. Neither row cites the sentence
that keeps the case out of row 9: `DOM-2`'s second sentence.

**Evidence**

- `SEC-42`: "Persistent malware, a poisoned build, a tampered dependency, or a wrench that begins
  mid-spend while the normal PIN is in RAM: any of these reads the normal PIN and substitutes it, so
  the Escape never arms, no node locks down".
- `SEC-42` again: "the coerced hot spend completes after the Hold".
- `SEC-54` row 9:
  - attacker: "the wrench: the user, `U` `P` `D` `C`";
  - outcome: "Denial: duress sweeps to the escape wallet at `T`, Lockdown follows";
  - enforced at: `05` and `SEC-8`.
- `SEC-54` row 8:
  - attacker: "coordinator host pre-wrench (`C`, reads `P`, `U` while software)";
  - outcome: "Bounded theft: hot spends up to the budget, and duress is nullified by PIN
    substitution".
- `SEC-54`'s preamble says that host "holds `C`, reads `P` when it is entered". A coordinator
  holding the normal PIN in RAM when the wrench begins has done exactly that.
- `DOM-2`: "Requirements that hold against a hostile coordinator are written for a coordinator that
  turns hostile AT the moment of coercion, holding the coordinator auth key but no history of the
  normal PIN." Neither row cites `DOM-2`.
- The class itself is deliberate, and this bead does not dispute it. Its uses:
  - the heading: "A coordinator compromised BEFORE the wrench nullifies duress";
  - ADR-0012 places "or a wrench that begins mid-spend while the normal pin is still in RAM" inside
    "a coordinator compromised *before* the wrench";
  - the executive summary: "none addresses a wrench that begins mid-spend (`SEC-42`)";
  - `OPS-47`: "addresses neither malware resident on a correctly built coordinator nor a wrench
    that begins mid-spend".

**Trace**

1. The Operator starts a hot spend. The coordinator holds the normal PIN in RAM, as `SEC-3`
   requires ("MUST hold it in RAM only").
2. Before that spend's request is done, a coercer takes the Operator and the coordinator host.
3. The coercer has the Operator enter a PIN, and the Operator enters the duress PIN.
4. The coordinator, now the coercer's, sends the normal PIN it already holds.

By `SEC-42`, "the Escape never arms, no node locks down". In the matrix:

- **Row 9's attacker cell fits.** The coercer holds the user, `U`, `P`, `D` and `C`. Row 9 says
  "Lockdown follows".
- **Row 8's attacker cell fits too.** The host holds `C`, read `P` when it was entered, and holds `U`
  while it is software. Row 8 says "duress is nullified by PIN substitution", which agrees with
  `SEC-42`. Its Operator cell lists `D`, which this coercer holds through the user.

Only `DOM-2`'s "no history of the normal PIN", which neither row cites, keeps the case out of
row 9.

**Not claimed**

- No new attack: `SEC-42` already states this history and its outcome.
- No claim that `DUR-1`'s node-observable equality fails. The coercer reads the PIN from the
  coordinator, not from a node.
- Row 9's outcome is not disputed for a wrench that begins with no normal PIN in RAM.
- No claim that `SEC-42`'s heading is false: the set uses "compromised before the wrench" for this
  case on purpose.
- No mitigation, gate or node behaviour changes.

**Done when**

1. Row 9's attacker is worded so it no longer fits a coercer who arrives while the normal PIN is in
   RAM, for example with `DOM-2`'s "no history of the normal PIN".
2. Optionally, the matrix names the mid-spend wrench explicitly, either in row 8's attacker cell
   or in a row of its own, with an outcome that agrees with `SEC-42`. Row 16 is precedent for a row
   defined by coordinator history.
3. Every other sentence that restates either row has been checked for agreement, and only what
   disagrees has changed.

title: Every claim of silence, a bound or a floor names the premises its theorem takes beside it, or says no theorem carries it (`AGENTS.md`, *Name the premises*)
description:
Type: task. Proposed priority: P2 (three of the four bugs filed on 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-20 are
this defect). Kind: requirement text and Lean docstrings; no behaviour change, no theorem change.
A gap the audit finds becomes its own bead.

`AGENTS.md`, *Name the premises*, landed with this bead, says a claim that a property holds
(silence, a bound, a floor) carries beside it the premises its theorem takes, in the theorem's
words, and a claim no theorem carries says so. `SEC-10` says it for silence: "The **scope of
SILENCE** MUST be stated wherever it is claimed". This bead applies the rule to the set as it
stands.

**Evidence** (all at `dd18bb6`)

- `bps-id2`: `bridge`'s docstring says "`hcohort` is what `countsAt_of_reserved` gives for any
  node that reserved inside its own interval", and the theorem concludes for a ledger that "has
  been through `POL-19`'s release and nothing else", not for a node's ledger in `sysRun`. The claim is stronger
  than the theorem.
- `bps-xyu`: `DUR-1` claims silence against one "holding the coordinator and the physical scene
  but no node"; `SEC-54` row 11 says "silence not claimed" for `n<t` node keys. Two statements of
  one claim draw different boundaries.
- `bps-amt`: `SEC-54` row 9 says Lockdown follows a wrench that `SEC-42` says no node locks down
  on. A cell states an outcome without the premise it rests on.
- Where the claims live: the 53 `SEC` rows of `12-security-requirements.md`, of which only
  `SEC-37` cites a `BtcPolicy` declaration; the cells of `SEC-54`; `DUR-1`, `OVR-13`, `POL-20`;
  and the eight "Formal scope:" paragraphs of `04-spend-lifecycle.md` and
  `05-duress-and-lockdown.md`, which already carry a theorem's premises and are the shape to
  match.
- Where the rule came from: the Linked Specs convention (`rad:z2HR882B4c4mTdAgdt4SozpdeTuMf`,
  `skills/linked-specs-claims/SKILL.md`) writes every load-bearing property as one sentence plus
  its immediate assumptions and nothing else, and links an assumption proven elsewhere instead of
  restating it. The repo already does the second half (*Cite the owner*).

**Work**

1. List every claim: a sentence saying a property holds under some adversary or over some run.
   Start from `12-security-requirements.md`'s rows and `SEC-54`'s cells, then `DUR-1`, `OVR-13`,
   `POL-20`, then every "Formal scope:" paragraph.
2. For each, name the theorem (its `@[req]` tag or its exhibit) or write that no theorem carries
   it. Write the premises beside the claim in the words of the theorem's hypotheses. A premise
   another requirement owns is cited by identifier.
3. Where the claim is stronger than the theorem, or two statements of one claim draw different
   boundaries, file a bead per gap in the form of `bps-xyu`, `needs-triage`, citing this one. Do
   not decide the direction of the fix here.

**Not claimed**

- No theorem changes, and no claim is weakened or strengthened in this bead.
- No new gate. Whether a check can hold a premise sentence to its theorem's hypotheses is the
  pointer below.
- The `CNF` items are not in scope: a conformance item exercises a rule, it does not claim a
  property.

**Pointer, not part of this bead**

`check_copies.py` holds a figure to its declaration and `check_citations.py` holds a quote to a
requirement; nothing holds a prose premise to a Lean hypothesis. If the audit shows the premise
sentences take one shape, a note on this bead says what such a check would read, so a bead for it
can be written.

**Done when**

1. Every claim on the list carries its premises in its theorem's words and cites the theorem, or
   carries the sentence that no theorem carries it.
2. Each gap found is its own bead, `needs-triage`, citing this one.

title: Name the premises, security chapter, tables: each clause in `SEC-2` and its adversary table, and in `SEC-54` and its matrix, carries its theorem's premises or says no theorem carries it
description:
Type: task. Priority: P3. Kind: requirement text; no theorem, gate or behaviour change. A child
of `bps-axj.1`, made by the owner's 2026-10-23 pick for cutting the security chapter's audit,
"Child beads, three (Recommended)": "bps-axj.1 becomes the parent of three new beads: tables,
`SEC-1`/`SEC-3`–`SEC-31`, and `SEC-32`–`SEC-53`." Each is claimed, reviewed, replayed, pushed and
closed on its own, like any bead.

**Waits for** `bps-axj.2`, `bps-axj.3`, `bps-axj.4` and `bps-axj.5`: the bundle the owner took,
"Take them (Recommended)", says in its item 4 "The audit pieces wait until bps-axj.2–.5 have landed
(4–0, round 2), because .2 and .3 rewrite proof paragraphs that the audit's pointers quote." It also waits for `bps-x72`, by the same item: "the fixes bead lands before the
tables piece."

`AGENTS.md`, *Name the premises*: "A claim that a property holds — silence, a bound, a floor —
carries, beside it, the premises its theorem takes, in the theorem's words; a claim no theorem
carries says so." This bead applies that rule to the scope below and nothing else, by the Run
rules below.

**Scope:** `12-security-requirements.md`: `SEC-2`, its text and every row of its adversary table
(A1 to A9); and `SEC-54`, its text before the matrix (the digest-copy note included), every matrix
row (1 to 17 and L1 to L8) and its closing paragraph. 36 sites at `201224c`: the two requirements'
text, 9 rows and 25 rows.

**Measured** at `201224c`; re-measure at the base this bead starts from. No declaration in `tools/formal/` is tagged with `SEC-2` or `SEC-54`; the only `SEC`
id any declaration is tagged with is `SEC-37` (three `@[req "SEC-37"]` tags). W6 lists the
`SEC-54` rows whose status records a decision.

**Known items** (the Run rules' W8, as they fall in this scope): A2, which `bps-7tv` says "names no digest-copy premise", with row 1 under R3; row 9's
"`U` `P` `D`", where `P` is used in two senses.

**How claims are marked** (the bundle's item 1, taken): per clause, never per table or chapter, in
W2's forms for a clause no theorem carries and W3's for a pointer to a proof. No gate checks the
quote in W2's named form, so the Run greps each one against its sentence and lists it in the
closing comment.

**Run rules** (the bundle's item 2, taken: rules for the Run, never written into the
specification). Verbatim from the final reading round, without its title line. The owner picked
"Point to the rule (Recommended)" for the digest-copy note, so W8's last item does not apply.
W7's "fixes bead" is `bps-x72`.

These rules apply `AGENTS.md`'s *Name the premises*: "A claim that a property holds — silence, a bound, a floor —
carries, beside it, the premises its theorem takes, in the theorem's words; a claim no theorem carries says so." They
also apply "A premise another requirement owns is cited, not restated." and *Quote the sentence*: "A claim about what
another requirement says carries that requirement's own words."

**W1. The unit is a claim, not a site.** A claim is one clause that says a property holds: silence, a bound, a floor,
a refusal, or a reach. A row cell or paragraph holding several such clauses gets one sort per clause. A5, for example,
holds "cannot reach quorum", "the Hot bound is stated for `c < t` (`POL-20`)" and a silence clause that claims nothing.

**W2. Committed form for a clause no theorem carries.** In a table cell the clause carries "no theorem carries this"
inside its own parenthesis or clause; the form, if the W5 search at A2 found no theorem, would be "cannot produce a
valid request (`SPN-18`; no theorem carries this);". In prose, when the sentence holds one property clause, the
sentence "No theorem carries this." follows it. When it holds more than one, the added sentence names the clause in
its own words: No theorem carries "<the clause's words>". No gate checks that quote: bare, it belongs to no attribution; under the site's own id, it matches its own paragraph. So the
Run greps each one against the sentence and lists it in the closing comment. Each form covers only
the clause it names. For the part a W4 split leaves, it says "the rest" for "this", and "the rest of" before a named
clause: "no theorem carries the rest"; No theorem carries the rest of "<the clause's words>". No sentence, column or note may cover clauses it does not name: no per-table, per-section or
per-chapter form. (The owner dropped "everything not named as proved is only argued" because "It is false: a checked
proof covers the hot budget, but that rule never names it.")

**W3. Committed form for a pointer.** It names the owner and says which part of the clause that owner's formal scope
proves: the whole clause under C1, only the proved part under C1p. It quotes, in at least four words each so the
citation gate checks them, that scope's statement of what it proves and any limit that scope states and the clause
reaches. One example of the form, not a site's whole text: `DUR-8` says "proves absence of exposed quorum for the target message at input 0", "the cross-signer hypothesis is not proved for
arbitrary environment-supplied rows" and "this
proves neither BIP143 binding nor full per-input or per-rung finalizability". It never says "the theorems that carry
this" or anything else that asserts a theorem carries more of the clause than that scope proves.

**W4. Sort each clause in this order; the first case that fits wins.** A split below splits the sort and the added
annotations, never the clause's own wording.
- **C0. Not a claim that a property holds:** a definition, a duty, a trust statement, a report, or an admitted
  weakness with no bound. Nothing is added. A duty or trust sentence that also asserts a property is split, and the
  property clause is sorted.
- **C4. An identified disagreement:** the clause says more than every owner it could rest on says and more than every
  theorem the W5 search found proves; or it credits a named theorem with more than that theorem's stated scope; or two
  statements of one claim draw different boundaries. A proof that is only partial or absent is not by itself C4: it
  goes to C1p, C2, C3 or UNSURE. A difference R3 keeps as decided is not C4. No edit. File a bead (needs-triage,
  citing `bps-axj`) in the form of `bps-2pd`. Do not decide its direction.
- **C1. An owner the clause cites has a formal scope that proves the clause as stated.** The conclusion has to match,
  not merely the fact that the owner names some proof. The clause gets a W3 pointer, and no premise is restated.
- **C1p. The owner's formal scope proves only part of the clause.** `DUR-1` names `BtcPolicy.Silence`, yet says "That a
  key copy learns nothing more is argued here, not proved.". Split the clause: the proved part gets a W3 pointer,
  and the rest is sorted again from C4.
- **C2. A theorem carries the clause, or only part of it, but no cited owner's formal scope gives a C1 or C1p pointer
  for it.** Name the declaration and write its premises in the words of its hypotheses. A premise another requirement
  owns is cited by id, not restated. If only part, split the clause: the carried part takes this form and says, as W3 does, which part the declaration carries, and the rest is
  sorted again from C4.
- **C3. The W5 search is complete and found no theorem carrying the clause, or the part of it still to sort.** W2.
- **UNSURE. The W5 search cannot settle it.** No edit. List the clause in the closing comment and in one filed
  needs-triage bead citing `bps-axj`. An unfinished search never yields W2.

**W5. The search, before any C4, C1, C1p, C2, C3 or UNSURE; only C0 is sorted without it.** For each clause:
1. Collect the ids it cites, with ranges expanded (`` `POL-16`–`POL-20` `` is five ids). Follow each cited `SEC` id
   one hop to the ids it cites, and add the site's own id.
2. List every declaration `tools/formal/.lake/index.jsonl` maps to those ids.
3. List every `BtcPolicy.` name in those ids' Markdown text, and every Lean docstring that names one of the ids.
   Tags are not enough: some theorem and lemma declarations carry no `@[req]`, and `Silence.lean:16` names
   `SEC-10`'s "digest premise" though no declaration is tagged `SEC-10`.
4. Grep `tools/formal/` for the clause's terms.
5. Read each candidate's statement and hypotheses against the clause, following the definitions they use and the
   results they depend on, and the other declarations in the modules found, tagged or not. Coverage this leaves
   unexamined is UNSURE, not C3.

The closing comment records, site by site, the ids searched, the candidates found and why each was taken or rejected.

**W6. Rows whose status records a decision.** These are the `SEC-54` rows whose status column records a decision:
- dated: 6, 10, 11, 14, 16, L4, L5, L6, L7;
- reasoned and undated: 5, 8, 17, L8 (rows 5 and 8 cite `ADR-0003` and `ADR-0015`).

The rules for them:
- **R1.** The status column is never edited.
- **R2.** Beside such a row's outcome, the Run may add, besides R4's W2 and W3, only one of three things:
  - (a) a citation of a premise, by the id of the requirement that owns it and by that owner's own label, where the
    row already cites that owner or cites a requirement that names the premise, in the form A4 and row 9 use:
    "subject to `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise" and "digest premise"". A premise citation claims no proof;
  - (b) a declaration name with its hypotheses quoted, when that declaration carries the outcome as the row states it;
    a premise another requirement owns is cited by id, not restated, as in C2;
  - (c) a quote from the decision body of an ADR entry that records the row's decision and that no later entry
    supersedes, named by number or heading title; never a rejected alternative or a rationale. Earlier entries can be
    overridden: `ADR-0021` decision 2 says earlier assumptions are "superseded by the descriptor-choice decision
    below".

  Whatever the route, an addition that makes the decided outcome depend on a condition the decision neither stated
  nor adopted through an owning-requirement reference is a HARD STOP. A theorem's hypotheses alone do not show such
  adoption. For a condition reached through a reference, the closing comment quotes the decision text and names the
  reference chain. At a HARD STOP, file a bead and make no edit. No gate checks a quote attributed to an ADR or to a
  Lean hypothesis (`check_citations.py`: "ADRs are attribution sources, never alternative quotation evidence"), so the
  Run greps each one against its source and lists them in the closing comment.
- **R3.** A `SEC-54` row that names a `SEC-2` row `A`k in any column ("settled (`A`k)", or row 15's "`SEC-38`, `A8`")
  is compared with that row clause by clause:
  - a premise added to a clause the two share goes into both, in the same words, or, if R2 stops it at the `SEC-54`
    row, into neither, and a bead is filed;
  - a difference an owner decided is kept (A5 is about "compromised nodes", row 11 about "a copy of the keys that runs
    no node");
  - any other difference is filed under C4, never aligned by the Run.
- **R4.** W2 and W3 may be added to any row, beside the clause they describe. They record what is proved, never what was
  decided, and never bypass C4 or R2's HARD STOP.

**W7. Texts decided outside these Runs.** The fixes bead lands before the tables piece. Its texts at A5, row 11, the
`SEC-54` digest-copy note, the "needed a PIN" sentence in `SEC-54`'s closing paragraph and `SPN-16` are taken as they then stand: the Run
sorts their clauses but rewords none of them. A5's silence clause, "silence is NOT claimed against them (`SEC-10`)",
was left by the owner and is never edited.

**W8. Known items handed to the pieces (no text now):**
- A2, which `bps-7tv` says "names no digest-copy premise", with row 1 under R3;
- row 9's "`U` `P` `D`", where `P` is used in two senses;
- `SEC-26`, which `bps-7tv` says "names no digest-copy case";
- `SEC-9`'s "the gate is the sole egress", which `DUR-8` also says, against `DUR-8`'s formal scope "the target message
  at input 0" (sorted by W4);
- only if the owner leaves the digest-copy note as it stands: that note, beside A2 under R3, marked as the owner's text,
  with no edit without the owner's word.

**Work**

1. Sort every claim in the scope by W1 to W6, and make only the edits they allow.
2. File a bead for each C4, each UNSURE and each R2 HARD STOP, `needs-triage`, citing `bps-axj`.
   Do not decide its direction.

**Not claimed** (`bps-axj`'s, unchanged)

- No theorem changes, and no claim is weakened or strengthened in this bead.
- No new gate. The note on the gate pointer stays on `bps-axj`.
- The `CNF` items are not in scope: a conformance item exercises a rule, it does not claim a
  property.
- `SEC-1` and `SEC-3` to `SEC-53` are `bps-axj.1.2`'s and `bps-axj.1.3`'s.

**Done when**

1. Every claim in the scope is sorted, and each carries its W3 pointer, its C2 declaration and
   premises, or its W2 form, or is C0, or is filed as item 2 says.
2. Each bead filed is `needs-triage` and cites `bps-axj`.
3. The closing comment records, site by site, the ids searched, the candidates found and why each
   was taken or rejected (W5). It lists every W2 named-form quote and every quote attributed to an
   ADR or a Lean hypothesis, each with its grep result (W2, R2), and for a condition reached
   through a reference it quotes the decision text and names the reference chain (R2).
4. The gate is green unpiped.

**HARD STOPS** (each needs the owner; never settle by consultation):

1. R2's: an addition that would make a decided outcome depend on a condition the decision neither
   stated nor adopted through an owning-requirement reference. File a bead and make no edit.
2. If a reviewer asks to edit a status column (R1), or to reword a text W7 names, A5's silence
   clause included, stop and report.
3. If the full gate is red on the final tree, stop and report its output.

title: Name the premises, security chapter, `SEC-1` and `SEC-3` to `SEC-31`: each claim carries its theorem's premises or says no theorem carries it
description:
Type: task. Priority: P3. Kind: requirement text; no theorem, gate or behaviour change. A child
of `bps-axj.1`, made by the owner's 2026-10-23 pick for cutting the security chapter's audit,
"Child beads, three (Recommended)": "bps-axj.1 becomes the parent of three new beads: tables,
`SEC-1`/`SEC-3`–`SEC-31`, and `SEC-32`–`SEC-53`." Each is claimed, reviewed, replayed, pushed and
closed on its own, like any bead.

**Waits for** `bps-axj.2`, `bps-axj.3`, `bps-axj.4` and `bps-axj.5`: the bundle the owner took,
"Take them (Recommended)", says in its item 4 "The audit pieces wait until bps-axj.2–.5 have landed
(4–0, round 2), because .2 and .3 rewrite proof paragraphs that the audit's pointers quote."

`AGENTS.md`, *Name the premises*: "A claim that a property holds — silence, a bound, a floor —
carries, beside it, the premises its theorem takes, in the theorem's words; a claim no theorem
carries says so." This bead applies that rule to the scope below and nothing else, by the Run
rules below.

**Scope:** `12-security-requirements.md`: `SEC-1` and every `SEC` requirement from `SEC-3` to
`SEC-31` (30 at `201224c`).

**Measured** at `201224c`; re-measure at the base this bead starts from. No declaration in `tools/formal/` is tagged with a `SEC` id in this scope; the only
`SEC` id any declaration is tagged with is `SEC-37` (three `@[req "SEC-37"]` tags).

**Known items** (the Run rules' W8, as they fall in this scope): `SEC-26`, which `bps-7tv` says "names no digest-copy case"; `SEC-9`'s "the gate is the
sole egress", which `DUR-8` also says, against `DUR-8`'s formal scope "the target message at input
0" (sorted by W4).

**How claims are marked** (the bundle's item 1, taken): per clause, never per table or chapter, in
W2's forms for a clause no theorem carries and W3's for a pointer to a proof. No gate checks the
quote in W2's named form, so the Run greps each one against its sentence and lists it in the
closing comment.

**Run rules** (the bundle's item 2, taken: rules for the Run, never written into the
specification). Verbatim from the final reading round, without its title line. The owner picked
"Point to the rule (Recommended)" for the digest-copy note, so W8's last item does not apply.
W7's "fixes bead" is `bps-x72`.

These rules apply `AGENTS.md`'s *Name the premises*: "A claim that a property holds — silence, a bound, a floor —
carries, beside it, the premises its theorem takes, in the theorem's words; a claim no theorem carries says so." They
also apply "A premise another requirement owns is cited, not restated." and *Quote the sentence*: "A claim about what
another requirement says carries that requirement's own words."

**W1. The unit is a claim, not a site.** A claim is one clause that says a property holds: silence, a bound, a floor,
a refusal, or a reach. A row cell or paragraph holding several such clauses gets one sort per clause. A5, for example,
holds "cannot reach quorum", "the Hot bound is stated for `c < t` (`POL-20`)" and a silence clause that claims nothing.

**W2. Committed form for a clause no theorem carries.** In a table cell the clause carries "no theorem carries this"
inside its own parenthesis or clause; the form, if the W5 search at A2 found no theorem, would be "cannot produce a
valid request (`SPN-18`; no theorem carries this);". In prose, when the sentence holds one property clause, the
sentence "No theorem carries this." follows it. When it holds more than one, the added sentence names the clause in
its own words: No theorem carries "<the clause's words>". No gate checks that quote: bare, it belongs to no attribution; under the site's own id, it matches its own paragraph. So the
Run greps each one against the sentence and lists it in the closing comment. Each form covers only
the clause it names. For the part a W4 split leaves, it says "the rest" for "this", and "the rest of" before a named
clause: "no theorem carries the rest"; No theorem carries the rest of "<the clause's words>". No sentence, column or note may cover clauses it does not name: no per-table, per-section or
per-chapter form. (The owner dropped "everything not named as proved is only argued" because "It is false: a checked
proof covers the hot budget, but that rule never names it.")

**W3. Committed form for a pointer.** It names the owner and says which part of the clause that owner's formal scope
proves: the whole clause under C1, only the proved part under C1p. It quotes, in at least four words each so the
citation gate checks them, that scope's statement of what it proves and any limit that scope states and the clause
reaches. One example of the form, not a site's whole text: `DUR-8` says "proves absence of exposed quorum for the target message at input 0", "the cross-signer hypothesis is not proved for
arbitrary environment-supplied rows" and "this
proves neither BIP143 binding nor full per-input or per-rung finalizability". It never says "the theorems that carry
this" or anything else that asserts a theorem carries more of the clause than that scope proves.

**W4. Sort each clause in this order; the first case that fits wins.** A split below splits the sort and the added
annotations, never the clause's own wording.
- **C0. Not a claim that a property holds:** a definition, a duty, a trust statement, a report, or an admitted
  weakness with no bound. Nothing is added. A duty or trust sentence that also asserts a property is split, and the
  property clause is sorted.
- **C4. An identified disagreement:** the clause says more than every owner it could rest on says and more than every
  theorem the W5 search found proves; or it credits a named theorem with more than that theorem's stated scope; or two
  statements of one claim draw different boundaries. A proof that is only partial or absent is not by itself C4: it
  goes to C1p, C2, C3 or UNSURE. A difference R3 keeps as decided is not C4. No edit. File a bead (needs-triage,
  citing `bps-axj`) in the form of `bps-2pd`. Do not decide its direction.
- **C1. An owner the clause cites has a formal scope that proves the clause as stated.** The conclusion has to match,
  not merely the fact that the owner names some proof. The clause gets a W3 pointer, and no premise is restated.
- **C1p. The owner's formal scope proves only part of the clause.** `DUR-1` names `BtcPolicy.Silence`, yet says "That a
  key copy learns nothing more is argued here, not proved.". Split the clause: the proved part gets a W3 pointer,
  and the rest is sorted again from C4.
- **C2. A theorem carries the clause, or only part of it, but no cited owner's formal scope gives a C1 or C1p pointer
  for it.** Name the declaration and write its premises in the words of its hypotheses. A premise another requirement
  owns is cited by id, not restated. If only part, split the clause: the carried part takes this form and says, as W3 does, which part the declaration carries, and the rest is
  sorted again from C4.
- **C3. The W5 search is complete and found no theorem carrying the clause, or the part of it still to sort.** W2.
- **UNSURE. The W5 search cannot settle it.** No edit. List the clause in the closing comment and in one filed
  needs-triage bead citing `bps-axj`. An unfinished search never yields W2.

**W5. The search, before any C4, C1, C1p, C2, C3 or UNSURE; only C0 is sorted without it.** For each clause:
1. Collect the ids it cites, with ranges expanded (`` `POL-16`–`POL-20` `` is five ids). Follow each cited `SEC` id
   one hop to the ids it cites, and add the site's own id.
2. List every declaration `tools/formal/.lake/index.jsonl` maps to those ids.
3. List every `BtcPolicy.` name in those ids' Markdown text, and every Lean docstring that names one of the ids.
   Tags are not enough: some theorem and lemma declarations carry no `@[req]`, and `Silence.lean:16` names
   `SEC-10`'s "digest premise" though no declaration is tagged `SEC-10`.
4. Grep `tools/formal/` for the clause's terms.
5. Read each candidate's statement and hypotheses against the clause, following the definitions they use and the
   results they depend on, and the other declarations in the modules found, tagged or not. Coverage this leaves
   unexamined is UNSURE, not C3.

The closing comment records, site by site, the ids searched, the candidates found and why each was taken or rejected.

**W6. Rows whose status records a decision.** These are the `SEC-54` rows whose status column records a decision:
- dated: 6, 10, 11, 14, 16, L4, L5, L6, L7;
- reasoned and undated: 5, 8, 17, L8 (rows 5 and 8 cite `ADR-0003` and `ADR-0015`).

The rules for them:
- **R1.** The status column is never edited.
- **R2.** Beside such a row's outcome, the Run may add, besides R4's W2 and W3, only one of three things:
  - (a) a citation of a premise, by the id of the requirement that owns it and by that owner's own label, where the
    row already cites that owner or cites a requirement that names the premise, in the form A4 and row 9 use:
    "subject to `SEC-10`'s "release-history premise" and "digest premise"". A premise citation claims no proof;
  - (b) a declaration name with its hypotheses quoted, when that declaration carries the outcome as the row states it;
    a premise another requirement owns is cited by id, not restated, as in C2;
  - (c) a quote from the decision body of an ADR entry that records the row's decision and that no later entry
    supersedes, named by number or heading title; never a rejected alternative or a rationale. Earlier entries can be
    overridden: `ADR-0021` decision 2 says earlier assumptions are "superseded by the descriptor-choice decision
    below".

  Whatever the route, an addition that makes the decided outcome depend on a condition the decision neither stated
  nor adopted through an owning-requirement reference is a HARD STOP. A theorem's hypotheses alone do not show such
  adoption. For a condition reached through a reference, the closing comment quotes the decision text and names the
  reference chain. At a HARD STOP, file a bead and make no edit. No gate checks a quote attributed to an ADR or to a
  Lean hypothesis (`check_citations.py`: "ADRs are attribution sources, never alternative quotation evidence"), so the
  Run greps each one against its source and lists them in the closing comment.
- **R3.** A `SEC-54` row that names a `SEC-2` row `A`k in any column ("settled (`A`k)", or row 15's "`SEC-38`, `A8`")
  is compared with that row clause by clause:
  - a premise added to a clause the two share goes into both, in the same words, or, if R2 stops it at the `SEC-54`
    row, into neither, and a bead is filed;
  - a difference an owner decided is kept (A5 is about "compromised nodes", row 11 about "a copy of the keys that runs
    no node");
  - any other difference is filed under C4, never aligned by the Run.
- **R4.** W2 and W3 may be added to any row, beside the clause they describe. They record what is proved, never what was
  decided, and never bypass C4 or R2's HARD STOP.

**W7. Texts decided outside these Runs.** The fixes bead lands before the tables piece. Its texts at A5, row 11, the
`SEC-54` digest-copy note, the "needed a PIN" sentence in `SEC-54`'s closing paragraph and `SPN-16` are taken as they then stand: the Run
sorts their clauses but rewords none of them. A5's silence clause, "silence is NOT claimed against them (`SEC-10`)",
was left by the owner and is never edited.

**W8. Known items handed to the pieces (no text now):**
- A2, which `bps-7tv` says "names no digest-copy premise", with row 1 under R3;
- row 9's "`U` `P` `D`", where `P` is used in two senses;
- `SEC-26`, which `bps-7tv` says "names no digest-copy case";
- `SEC-9`'s "the gate is the sole egress", which `DUR-8` also says, against `DUR-8`'s formal scope "the target message
  at input 0" (sorted by W4);
- only if the owner leaves the digest-copy note as it stands: that note, beside A2 under R3, marked as the owner's text,
  with no edit without the owner's word.

**Work**

1. Sort every claim in the scope by W1 to W6, and make only the edits they allow.
2. File a bead for each C4, each UNSURE and each R2 HARD STOP, `needs-triage`, citing `bps-axj`.
   Do not decide its direction.

**Not claimed** (`bps-axj`'s, unchanged)

- No theorem changes, and no claim is weakened or strengthened in this bead.
- No new gate. The note on the gate pointer stays on `bps-axj`.
- The `CNF` items are not in scope: a conformance item exercises a rule, it does not claim a
  property.
- `SEC-2` and `SEC-54` are `bps-axj.1.1`'s; `SEC-32` to `SEC-53` are `bps-axj.1.3`'s.

**Done when**

1. Every claim in the scope is sorted, and each carries its W3 pointer, its C2 declaration and
   premises, or its W2 form, or is C0, or is filed as item 2 says.
2. Each bead filed is `needs-triage` and cites `bps-axj`.
3. The closing comment records, site by site, the ids searched, the candidates found and why each
   was taken or rejected (W5). It lists every W2 named-form quote and every quote attributed to an
   ADR or a Lean hypothesis, each with its grep result (W2, R2), and for a condition reached
   through a reference it quotes the decision text and names the reference chain (R2).
4. The gate is green unpiped.

**HARD STOPS** (each needs the owner; never settle by consultation):

1. R2's: an addition that would make a decided outcome depend on a condition the decision neither
   stated nor adopted through an owning-requirement reference. File a bead and make no edit.
2. If a reviewer asks to edit a status column (R1), or to reword a text W7 names, A5's silence
   clause included, stop and report.
3. If the full gate is red on the final tree, stop and report its output.

`git diff e63715d 14611b0 --stat -- 05-duress-and-lockdown.md tools/formal` printed nothing, so the chapter and the formal layer are as the bead measured them. Two of the bead's **Measured** sentences were wrong:

comments.text:
Post-close review of this bead (a counterexample trace and a two-axis review, each in its own clone, then a fresh reader of the fix). Parts of two claims in scope, four in all, were neither credited nor disclaimed, and one rendering had drifted. Commit `1ca0cc4` fixes them in `05-duress-and-lockdown.md`. Every base word is kept in order, the change is inside `DUR-1` and the `decisionStart` paragraph, and no claim changes.

1. `DUR-1`: the credit to `BtcPolicy.Silence.silence` stops where the walk stops, but its no-theorem sentence named observables only. It now also says that on a trace no theorem carries anything from the step at which that walk stops through the rest of the trace or a run, except, where it stops at the trace's first step, what `BtcPolicy.Silence.obsOf_eq`, `BtcPolicy.Silence.respond_pub` and `BtcPolicy.Silence.markerOf_pub` prove from the given initial states.

No kernel transition emits this node's relays (`NCH-27`). `BtcPolicy.Silence.work` is empty for every event other than an acceptance and a holder decision. The `decisionStart` paragraph: `BtcPolicy.Silence.inv_step` and `BtcPolicy.Silence.inv_sysStep` carry part of the shared-window write (`BtcPolicy.Silence.NodeInv.windows`, `BtcPolicy.Silence.NodeInv.selWin`) only under their premises. - `bps-mgqf` no longer says "no behaviour change" or "No theorem, gate, observer projection or node behaviour changes here." Narrowing `DUR-1`'s list to `SEC-10`'s would change what a node must keep identical, so both fit one direction only.

comments.author: Allan Douglas
comments.text:
Second post-close fix, in `f570be6`. The itemized form of `DUR-1`'s no-theorem sentence did not converge. Independent reads of the silence credits and the disclaimer, each testing every sentence in both directions against the formal model, found 6 blocking points in the text at `179aab4` (lines 20-50), then 4 and 3 in two successive fixes that only added words, the later findings mostly in the words the fix before had added. The disclaimer now takes the group 5 committed form for the part of a clause no theorem carries ("For the part a W4 split leaves, it says "the rest" for "this", and "the rest of" before a named clause: "no theorem carries the rest"; No theorem carries the rest of "<the clause's words>"."): the "nothing ... except" list is replaced by "No theorem carries the rest of this silence clause.", followed by examples. Decided under that rule without a new owner question; the owner may overrule it.

Kept from the fixes, which the later reads found correct:
- `BtcPolicy.Silence.pending_pub` and `BtcPolicy.Silence.pub_lockedDown` are credited for the pending listing and the Lockdown latch of coupled initial states before any step.
- The first-step credit for `BtcPolicy.Silence.obsOf_eq` names its `BtcPolicy.Silence.NodeInv` premise, and "each whatever the horizon" now reads "each of the last two whatever the horizon": `obsOf_eq` takes both horizons.
- The review note on starts outside `BtcPolicy.Silence.silence`'s initial-state premises: the text says what the premises of `silence` and of `BtcPolicy.Silence.silence_initial` reach, and that from coupled starts outside both, for example one `BtcPolicy.Kernel.Reachable.init` state with its sweep flag set taken in both runs, `BtcPolicy.Silence.markerOf_pub` and `BtcPolicy.Silence.respond_pub` carry the first step's confirmation marker and response. Everything else from such starts falls under "the rest".

The examples are items no read challenged: response bytes, the bytes of the `/pending` and `/healthz` bodies, response timing class, `/events`, the other `/healthz` fields, peer message sizes, a queued partial's destinations and its transmission, lock and allocation counts, store-lock hold time, and steps the formal kernel has no event for (a refresh's or a claw-back's ingress, the deadline driver's pass), with anything after one. Dropped rather than repaired, since a read challenged each: the landed exceptions for other peer messages and for candidate visits, and a draft sentence on the refusal code a staged-refusal input carries. "The rest" covers what each had left out.

Evidence:
- Every changed word is inside `DUR-1`; the `decisionStart` paragraph is unchanged.
- A search of every general declaration whose conclusion could state part of the silence clause found none that states a part the credits do not name. It covered each theorem whose statement has a coupling, two enrolment tables or two duress bits; each theorem tagged with a `DUR`, `DEF-12`, `SEC-10`, `API` or `NCH` id or with `SPN-5`, `SPN-30` or `SPN-38`; and each general theorem on the response, the marker, the work, the pending listing, the latch or a step's effects. The two-run lemmas that conclude a step's effects or work (`BtcPolicy.Silence.sysStep_coupled`, `BtcPolicy.Silence.step_pub`, `BtcPolicy.Silence.firePass_pub`, `BtcPolicy.Silence.send_pub`, `BtcPolicy.Silence.work_pub`) take `NodeInv` and both horizons at that step, as `obsOf_eq` does, or (`work_pub`) the leaving states' coupling. The other one-step lemmas conclude a node projection, or a ledger or admission function. Fixed-trace exhibits were not counted, as in the earlier reads.
- A fresh reader, who had read none of the earlier drafts or their reviews, checked the final text in both directions (a credit no proof carries; a declaration's conclusion that "the rest" or an example takes in) and each kept credit's premises and stopping point against its declaration: no blocking finding.
- The full gate passed on the edited tree.

Notes for the owner from that read, none blocking:
1. "from their coupling alone" is said of `BtcPolicy.Silence.pending_pub` and `BtcPolicy.Silence.pub_lockedDown`, which take only equal node projections, and also of `BtcPolicy.Silence.respond_pub`, which takes the whole coupling, ledger included. True, but it does not name the narrower premise.
2. The unchanged sentence "Thus the coupling and model-invariant premises narrow none of those same-state starts with the sweep flag clear." now sits beside the new statement that `silence`'s premises reach only states satisfying `NodeInv`. A same-state start with its sweep flag clear and `T` not equal to its `unarmedT` fails `NodeInv`; `silence_initial` still carries it, so the old sentence holds only as "no such start is left without the relation".
3. The examples no longer name peer message shapes or candidate visits, which `BtcPolicy.Silence.Obs` carries only in part (its effects are queued partials and broadcasts; `BtcPolicy.Silence.work` lists only an acceptance's and a holder decision's visits). "The rest" covers both.

title: OPS-25 and OPS-63 have the node-lifecycle drill restore a node from backup, which STO-1's default one-shot nodes rule out ("A dead node never rejoins")
description:
Type: bug. Proposed priority: P3 (a drill step the default design cannot perform, and a sentence
that says the drill does it; no node behaviour is affected). Kind: requirement text in `OPS-25` and
`OPS-63`. No node, wire or gate change.

The backup rule says the node-lifecycle drill restores a node (`OPS-25`): "A backup that has never
been restored from is a hypothesis. The recovery drill (`OPS-27`) restores from cold artifacts
alone; the node-lifecycle drill (`OPS-63`) restores a node; the custody drill (`OPS-61`) restores
key material from backups alone. They are different backups with different failure modes and MUST
NOT be merged into one harness."

The drill's second step asks for it (`OPS-63`): "(1) reboot a node and confirm it is dead exactly as
`ADR-0007` claims; (2) restore from backup onto a fresh machine; (3) lose quorum and recover;". The
same requirement ends: "Afterwards every operational document MUST point at the chosen model and no
procedure may remain that a sealed node cannot perform."

The default node lifecycle forbids it (`STO-1`): "A node therefore starts exactly once in its life
(`MAN-36`). A dead node never rejoins: reprovisioning with the same key and manifest is the
resurrection `ADR-0007` rejects, and a new key is not in the immutable manifest. Restoring capacity
means rotating to a successor vault." `MAN-36` adds: "Once the node is up and the host sealed the
operator MUST destroy the paper preimage". `OPS-61` already says its own drill "does not restore a
node (`OPS-63`)".

So an Operator who runs the drill on the default design reaches step (2) with nothing that can
restore a node, and `OPS-25` states as done what that step cannot do.

**Owner decision 2026-10-21:** file it. Reword so the drill confirms the dead machine cannot come
back, then rebuilds capacity with a new vault.

**Direction** (exact text left to triage):

- `OPS-63` step (2), under the default lifecycle (`OPS-62` (a)): confirm that the dead node cannot
  rejoin, then restore capacity by rotating to a successor vault (`STO-1`).
- `OPS-25`: the node-lifecycle drill confirms that a dead node cannot rejoin and restores capacity
  through rotation, in place of "restores a node".
- The rewording must not settle `F8` ("the node lifecycle decision waits on stage-4 attrition
  data"). It states the step for the specified default only. If `OPS-62`'s ADR chooses recoverable
  nodes (b), that ADR replaces the step, as `OPS-62` already requires ("the ADR MUST explicitly
  supersede or amend every document it contradicts").

**Evidence**

- Readers A, B and C of the 2026-10-19 panel on `bps-363` would reword the drill this way; A:
  "confirm that backups cannot resurrect the dead node, then restore capacity by rotating to a
  successor vault"; B: attempt the restore, "verify that the dead node cannot rejoin, and restore
  capacity by rotation". Reader D dropped `bps-363`'s change to the drill and left its text. The
  tension predates `bps-363`.

**Not claimed**

- `F8` and `OPS-62`'s choice are not decided or narrowed here.
- No other drill (`OPS-27`, `OPS-61`) changes.
close_reason: OPS-25 and OPS-63 now say the node-lifecycle drill, under the default lifecycle, confirms that a dead node cannot rejoin and restores capacity by rotation to a successor vault (STO-1), which is step (4)'s migration; both edits landed word for word in 39cd596, OPS-27, OPS-61 and OPS-62 unchanged, every gate green

title: SPN-41's removal: pin the effective-time close with an exhibit and a control; ADR-0027's 'only'

title: check_formal.sh's req-attribute greps are lexical: multiline duplicate tags and multiline attribute [req] retags pass
description:
`tools/check_formal.sh:45-49` refuses a declaration tagged `@[req]` twice and an after-the-fact `attribute [req …]` with two greps. Both are lexical: the first requires the literal spacing `req "` (a newline between `req` and the string defeats `\breq "`), and the second is per-line (`grep -rnE`), so `attribute [\n  req "CHN-4"\n] name` is not seen. Lean accepts both multiline forms; the runtime gate then sees only the effective (last) tag and passes, so a declaration can be silently retagged. Reported by reviewer D; not yet reproduced — reproduce first.

Repair, smallest that works: make both greps whitespace-tolerant and file-spanning — `-z` on the attribute check as well, `\breq\s+"` in place of `\breq "` (the multiline implemented_by check at line 37 is the pattern to copy). Add two negative controls in `.github/workflows/gates.yml` beside the existing "implemented_by … written over several lines" control: a multiline duplicate `@[req\n "CHN-4", req\n "CHN-2"]` tag and a multiline `attribute [\n req "…"\n]` retag, each red at the named message. Do not move these checks into the Lean gate unless the grep cannot express them.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both multiline forms are red at `check_formal.sh` with the existing messages.
- Two new gates.yml steps prove it, runnable locally.
- KEEP working: the single-line forms still red (existing behaviour); a legitimate `@[req "X"] def …` and a docstring containing the word `req` still pass; `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` green on the final tree.
- Files: `tools/check_formal.sh`, `.github/workflows/gates.yml`. No other files.

title: Formal: move bps-nfx's general proofs into Evaluate.lean, drop the hint seam and POL-10's dated tag
description:
This bead fixes three findings from the review of `bps-nfx` (`e5c0810`). None of them changes a
verdict or a theorem statement.

## Findings

1. **General proofs live in `Exhibits.lean`.** `ADR-0023` keeps each model's general proofs in
   its own module. `Exhibits.lean` holds the `current` instantiations and the executable verdicts
   (decision 6, decision 12 and Consequences: "`BtcPolicy/Exhibits.lean` holds the current
   exhibits"). Its other theorems with general binders are all `_with_current` instantiations of
   proofs owned elsewhere.

   `bps-nfx` instead put these general proofs under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`:
   - `softenCode`, `FirstAt`;
   - `hints_never_admit`, `hints_acceptance_iff`;
   - `recognised_iff`;
   - `firstUnknown_none_iff`, `firstUnknown_some_iff`;
   - `allowlisted_iff`;
   - `dest_allowed_iff`, `dest_notAllowed_iff`, `dest_changeNotDerivable_iff`;
   - `acceptance_exact`, `first_failing_output`.

   `POL-6`'s formal-home sentence therefore points into `Exhibits`. The cause was `bps-nfx`'s own
   control clause, which named "theorem 2 and the hinted-stranger exhibit" in one build. That
   clause is withdrawn here.
2. **`recognised` takes a `_hint` argument it never reads.** Its docstring says the argument
   exists only for the negative control, so the definition is shaped by its test.
3. **`POL-10` ends "(amended 2026-10-05)".** README forbids inline dated tags ("The reference
   project kept every correction inline with a dated tag, and its documents became hard to
   read"). No earlier value exists, because `POL-10` was silent on the case before.

## Scope

- **Move the general proofs listed in finding 1** into `tools/formal/BtcPolicy/Evaluate.lean`,
  namespace `BtcPolicy.Evaluate`, without changing their statements. The decided exhibits stay in
  `Exhibits.lean`, under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`: `cfg`, `accepted`, `consistencyRows`,
  `fixture_membership`, the `POL-7` rows, `foreign_input`, the stranger exhibits,
  `hot_budget_refused` and the two fee exhibits.
- **Drop `_hint` from `recognised`.** `recognised_iff` loses its hint argument.
- **Move the mutation seam into `firstUnknown`.** Its `if recognised …` line carries a trailing
  `-- hint-trust` marker, and the `gates.yml` control's `sed` adds `|| hs.headD false` to that
  condition.
- **Rewrite the control so its errors fall in `Evaluate.lean`.** It must name
  `hints_never_admit`. Measure the exact count with
  `nix develop --command python3 .context/latch/run-steps.py <name>` and pin the measured value.
  The decided exhibit is no longer part of the control, since `Exhibits.lean` cannot build once
  `Evaluate.lean` fails. Keep it in one shard.
- **Rewrite the docstrings written around the test.** These are `Evaluate.lean`'s module
  docstring ("The planted hint-trust mutation must leave this upstream module buildable…") and
  `hints_never_admit`'s "independently of all mutation-sensitive characterisation lemmas". A
  docstring states what the declaration says, not how CI breaks it.
- **Update `POL-6`'s formal-home sentence** to the `BtcPolicy.Evaluate.*` names.
- **Delete "(amended 2026-10-05)" from `POL-10`.** The rest of the sentence stays verbatim, since
  `CNF-17` quotes it.

## Out of scope

Any change to a theorem statement, an exhibit's verdict, `request`, `evaluate`, or the
`CNF-17`/`POL-10` rule. Leave the other dated tags in `ADR-0020` and `05-duress-and-lockdown.md`
alone.

## Done when

- The three findings are fixed.
- No general proof remains under `BtcPolicy.Exhibits.Evaluate`.
- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` is green, run unpiped.
- The rewritten control passes locally with its measured count.
- Every other `gates.yml` control whose count or line moves is re-run with `run-steps.py` and
  updated to the measured value. This includes the `DEF-15`, `F57` and citation declaration-name
  controls.
