title: Every relay carries the plaintext PIN over node-to-node links, and only OPS-50's coordinator ingress is required to be confidential
description:
Type: bug. Proposed priority: P3 (neither mechanism `F37` names would carry a relay in clear, but a
link that meets `OPS-51` as written can, and the PIN it carries is what `OPS-50` already protects on
the first hop). Kind: requirement text in `OPS-51` and `NCH-2`'s stage-2 sentence, with a
verification like `OPS-50`'s. No other node or wire change.

The coordinator sends a spend request, PIN included, to one node over an ingress that `OPS-50`
requires to be confidential: "It MUST be confidential because a spend request carries the plaintext
PIN". That node relays the same bytes to every peer (`NCH-27`): "The relay carries the coordinator's
bytes verbatim, PIN included, which is why its contents are pin-dependent by construction and only
its presence and length are uniform." The node-to-node link has no confidentiality requirement:

- `OPS-51`: "From stage 2 node-to-node transport MUST be routable and authenticated, with the
  manifest-pinned endpoints (`MAN-4`) and the channel-key endorsements (`NCH-5`) doing the
  authentication".
- `NCH-2`: "Transport is HTTP POST to `http://<endpoint>/channel` at each peer's manifest-pinned
  endpoints (`MAN-4`)", and "from stage 2 the transport is routable and authenticated (`OPS-51`)".
- `NCH-5`: "possession of the channel key is proven per message by the envelope signature", which
  a link in clear also meets.

Only `OPS-50` requires confidentiality today; the word appears nowhere else in the set's
requirements. So a passive observer of one node-to-node link reads the normal PIN of every ordinary
spend, before any wrench. That is a record of the normal PIN: `bps-xyu`'s condition (decided
2026-10-21) excludes it for the holder of a copied node key, and `DUR-1`'s claim against the
coordinator at the wrench does not name it (`bps-axj`'s class).

**Evidence**

- Triage panel on `bps-363`, `bps-xyu` and `bps-amt`, 2026-10-21, last round: a bead, 4–0 (readers
  A–D). Both mechanisms `F37` lists, "onion addresses derived from node key material, or mTLS"
  (`OPS-51`), encrypt the link; no requirement says the link must be confidential.
- Stage 1 is unaffected: "At rollout stage 1 every endpoint is `127.0.0.1:<port>`" (`NCH-2`).

**Direction** (left to triage): the readers proposed that `OPS-51` require node-to-node transport
to be confidential as well as authenticated, for the reason `OPS-50` gives, with a check that a
relay's PIN is not readable on the link, whichever mechanism `F37` selects.

**Not claimed**

- No leak is shown in a deployment that uses either `F37` mechanism.
- The relay's presence and length stay uniform (`NCH-27`); only its contents are in question.
- `F37`'s choice of mechanism is not made here.
close_reason: OPS-51 now requires node-to-node transport from stage 2 to be routable, authenticated and confidential, because a relay carries the plaintext PIN (NCH-27), verified by a captured relay from which the PIN cannot be read even with payload_b64 decoded; NCH-2 and CNF-127 agree; all three edits landed word for word in 735ea8a, F37's choice unmade, API-1 and MAN-4 unchanged, every gate green

comments.author: Allan Douglas
comments.text:
Triage, 2026-10-21. Read by four independent readers, A–D, in three rounds against `eca04cf` with
this bead's text applied, alongside `bps-69r`'s and `bps-ay1`'s.

**Owner decision** (2026-10-21, verbatim): "Require it". Node-to-node transport from stage 2 MUST
also be confidential, with the reviewed text below in `OPS-51`, `NCH-2` and `CNF-127`.

**Correction to the description** (at `eca04cf`): "`DUR-1`'s claim against the coordinator at the
wrench does not name it" is stale. `bps-xyu` landed `SEC-10`'s "a holder of a record of either PIN
from any source can compare it with the PIN offered at the wrench (`DUR-1`)", and `DUR-1` now says
"Such a record is excluded whatever its source". A link observer's record of the normal PIN is such
a record. The requirement gap stands: `OPS-51` asks no confidentiality.

**Review**

- Earlier round (on `bps-363`, `bps-xyu`, `bps-amt`): a bead, and this direction, 4–0.
- Round 2, the text: OK, 4–0. Both mechanisms `F37` names encrypt, so the choice is not narrowed
  (D); the reason quotes `NCH-27`'s own relay sentence (C); `NCH-2`'s `http://` scheme beside mTLS
  is `F37`'s to settle (C).
- Round 3, the check: "does not show the PIN" would pass a cleartext link under a naive search,
  since the envelope's `payload_b64` is base64 (B). "the PIN cannot be read … even with
  `payload_b64` decoded": OK, 4–0. It concerns a link capture, not the endpoints, which still
  receive "the coordinator's bytes verbatim, PIN included" (A, B).

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug

**Summary:** From stage 2, node-to-node transport MUST be routable, authenticated and confidential
(`OPS-51`), because a relay carries the plaintext PIN, verified by a captured relay from which the
PIN cannot be read even with `payload_b64` decoded; `NCH-2` and `CNF-127` agree, and `F37`'s choice
of mechanism stays open.

**Current behavior:**
`OPS-51` says "From stage 2 node-to-node transport MUST be routable and authenticated", and `NCH-2`
says the same. Only `OPS-50` requires confidentiality, for the coordinator's ingress: "It MUST be
confidential because a spend request carries the plaintext PIN". A relay carries the same bytes to
every peer (`NCH-27`). The description has the evidence.

**Desired behavior:** these three edits, as written.

1. `OPS-51`, replacing "From stage 2 node-to-node transport MUST be routable and authenticated, with
   the manifest-pinned endpoints (`MAN-4`) and the channel-key endorsements (`NCH-5`) doing the
   authentication; clearnet" with: "From stage 2 node-to-node transport MUST be routable,
   authenticated and confidential, with the manifest-pinned endpoints (`MAN-4`) and the channel-key
   endorsements (`NCH-5`) doing the authentication. It MUST be confidential because, as `NCH-27`
   says, "The relay carries the coordinator's bytes verbatim, PIN included". Verification: the PIN
   cannot be read from a relay captured on a node-to-node link, even with `payload_b64` decoded.
   Clearnet".
2. `NCH-2`, replacing "from stage 2 the transport is routable and authenticated (`OPS-51`), and"
   with: "from stage 2 the transport is routable, authenticated and confidential (`OPS-51`), and".
3. `CNF-127`, replacing "the read-surface perimeter is recorded before the nodes are reachable; the
   diversity statement is attested." with: "the read-surface perimeter is recorded before the nodes
   are reachable; the PIN cannot be read from a relay captured on a node-to-node link, even with
   `payload_b64` decoded; the diversity statement is attested.".

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Edits 1 to 3 are applied as written; `OPS-51`'s sentence naming the mechanism as `F37` is
      unchanged.
- [ ] `API-1` and `MAN-4`, which cite `OPS-51`, are checked and left alone unless one now
      disagrees; the closing comment says what was checked.
- [ ] `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`, unpiped and redirected to a file, exits 0.

**Out of scope:**
- `F37`'s choice of mechanism ("onion addresses derived from node key material, or mTLS") is not
  made or narrowed.
- No node, wire or gate behaviour changes; stage 1 stays on `127.0.0.1` (`NCH-2`).
- The relay's contents at the endpoints are unchanged (`NCH-27`).

**HARD STOPS** (owner-only; never settle by consultation):
1. The requirement is the owner's: "Require it". If a reviewer asks to drop the confidentiality
   MUST, to make it a SHOULD, or to close the bead as a stated limit, stop and report.
2. If an edit seems to need `F37`'s choice of mechanism, stop and report.
3. If an edit, as written, makes false a theorem statement, an ADR decision or a requirement this
   brief does not touch, stop that part, finish the rest, and report it with the texts quoted
   (`AGENTS.md`, *When the set blocks the work*).

Comments on this bead are posted with `br comments add --author "Allan Douglas"`.

comments.author: Allan Douglas
comments.text:
